title.raw: 卷十七 列傳第五: 景穆十二王上 Volume 17 Biographies 5: Jingmu's Twelve Sons 1

sentences.zh: 景穆十二王上

translations.literal: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 1)

sentences.zh: 列傳第五景穆十二王上

translations.literal: Biographies 5: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 5 — Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 1)

sentences.zh: 景穆皇帝十四男：恭皇后生文成皇帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Jingmu had fourteen sons: the Gong Empress bore Emperor Wencheng;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu had fourteen sons. The Gong Empress bore Emperor Wencheng;

sentences.zh: 袁椒房生陽平幽王新成；

translations.literal: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Yangping the Somber, Xincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Yangping the Somber, Xincheng;

sentences.zh: 尉椒房生京兆康王子推、濟陰王小新成；

translations.literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Jingzhao the Kind, Zitui, and Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Jingzhao the Kind, Zitui, and the Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng;

sentences.zh: 陽椒房生汝陰靈王天賜；

translations.literal: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Ruyin the Spirited, Tianci;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Ruyin the Spirited, Tianci;

sentences.zh: 樂良厲王萬壽、廣平殤王洛侯母並闕。

translations.literal: the mothers of Prince of Leliang the Stern, Wanshou, and Prince of Guangping the Untimely, Luohou are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: the mothers of the Prince of Leliang the Stern, Wanshou, and the Prince of Guangping the Untimely, Luohou are unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 孟椒房生任城康王雲；

translations.literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Rencheng the Kind, Yun;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Rencheng the Kind, Yun;

sentences.zh: 劉椒房生南安惠王楨、城陽康王長壽。

translations.literal: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Nan'an the Graceful, Zhen, and Prince of Chengyang the Kind, Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Nan'an the Graceful, Zhen, and the Prince of Chengyang the Kind, Changshou.

sentences.zh: 慕容椒房生章武敬王太洛；

translations.literal: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Zhangwu the Revered, Tailuo;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Zhangwu the Revered, Tailuo;

sentences.zh: 尉椒房生樂陵康王胡兒；

translations.literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Leling the Kind, Hu'er;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Leling the Kind, Hu'er;

sentences.zh: 孟椒房生安定靖王休。

translations.literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Anding the Tranquil, Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Anding the Tranquil, Xiu.

sentences.zh: 趙王深早薨，無傳，母闕。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Shen died early; no biography; mother unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao, Shen, died in youth and has no biography; his mother is unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 魏舊太子後庭未有位號，文成即位，景穆宮人有子者，並號為椒房。

translations.literal: Under Wei custom the former crown prince's inner quarters had no rank titles; when Wencheng took the throne, palace women of Jingmu who had borne sons were all styled Pepper-Chamber consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei custom the former crown prince's inner quarters bore no rank titles. When Wencheng took the throne, every palace woman of Jingmu who had borne a son was styled a Pepper-Chamber consort.

sentences.zh: 陽平王新成，太安三年封，後為內都大官。

translations.literal: Prince of Yangping Xincheng was enfeoffed in the third year of Tai'an and later served as Grand Palace Official of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yangping, Xincheng, received his fief in the third year of Tai'an and later served as Grand Palace Official of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰幽。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Somber.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Somber.

sentences.zh: 長子安壽襲爵，孝文後賜名頤。

translations.literal: His eldest son Anshou succeeded to the title; Emperor Xiaowen later granted him the name Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Anshou succeeded to the title; Emperor Xiaowen later granted him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 累遷懷朔鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Huaishuo Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to General of Huaishuo Garrison.

sentences.zh: 都督三道諸軍事北討，詔征赴京，勖以戰伐之事。

translations.literal: As commander of the three-route armies on the northern campaign, he was summoned to the capital; the emperor exhorted him on matters of war.
translations.idiomatic: Made commander of the three-route armies on the northern campaign, he was summoned to the capital, where the emperor exhorted him on matters of war.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「當仰杖廟算，使呼韓同渭橋之禮。

translations.literal: He replied: "I shall rely on the plans of the ancestral temple and make the Hun submit as they did at Weiqiao."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "I shall rely on the plans of the ancestral temple and bring the Hun to submit as they did at Weiqiao."

sentences.zh: 」帝歎曰：「壯哉王言，朕所望也。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: "What bold words, Prince—just what I hoped to hear."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: "What bold words, Prince—just what I hoped to hear."

sentences.zh: 」未發，遭母憂，詔遣侍臣以金革敦喻，既殯而發。

translations.literal: Before he set out he was struck by his mother's death; an edict sent attendants to urge him with the doctrine of metal and leather—that war does not wait for mourning—and he marched after the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he was struck by his mother's death. An edict sent attendants to urge him with the doctrine of metal and leather—that war does not wait for mourning—and he marched after the burial.

sentences.zh: 與陸睿集三道諸將議軍途所詣。

translations.literal: With Lu Rui he gathered the generals of the three routes to deliberate which path the army should take.
translations.idiomatic: With Lu Rui he gathered the generals of the three routes to decide which path the army should take.

sentences.zh: 於是中道出黑山，東道趣士盧河，西道向侯延河。

translations.literal: The center route went through Black Mountain, the east route toward the Shilu River, the west route toward the Houyan River.
translations.idiomatic: The center route went through Black Mountain, the east toward the Shilu River, the west toward the Houyan River.

sentences.zh: 軍過大磧，大破蠕蠕。

translations.literal: The army crossed the great desert and routed the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The army crossed the great desert and routed the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 頤入朝，詔曰：「王之前言，果不虛也。

translations.literal: When Yi came to court, the edict said: "Your words before, Prince, have indeed proved true."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi came to court, the edict said: "Your words before, Prince, have indeed proved true."

sentences.zh: 」後除朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made governor of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 及恆州刺史穆泰謀反，遣使推頤為主，頤密以狀聞。

translations.literal: When Governor of Hengzhou Mu Tai plotted rebellion, he sent envoys urging Yi as leader; Yi secretly reported the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the governor of Hengzhou, Mu Tai, plotted rebellion, he sent envoys urging Yi to lead them; Yi secretly reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 泰等伏誅，帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Tai and the rest were executed; the emperor greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and his accomplices were executed; the emperor greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 宣武景明元年，薨于青州刺史，諡曰莊王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingming under Emperor Xuanwu he died as governor of Qingzhou; posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingming under Emperor Xuanwu he died in office as governor of Qingzhou and was given the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫宗胤。

translations.literal: The fief passed to his grandson Zongyin.
translations.idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson Zongyin.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，坐殺叔父賜死，爵除。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming he was sentenced to death for killing his uncle; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was sentenced to death for killing his uncle; the title was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 頤弟衍，字安樂，賜爵廣陵侯，位梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Yan, styled Anle, was granted the title Marquis of Guangling and made governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yan, styled Anle, was granted the title Marquis of Guangling and made governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 表請假王，以崇威重。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking for a provisional kingship to enhance his authority.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized asking for a provisional kingship to enhance his authority.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「可謂無厭求也，所請不合。

translations.literal: The edict said: "This may be called insatiable ambition; the request is not granted."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "This may be called insatiable ambition; the request is not granted."

sentences.zh: 」轉徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 至州病重，帝敕徐成伯乘傳療疾。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he fell gravely ill; the emperor ordered Xu Chengbai to ride post-haste to treat him.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the province he fell gravely ill; the emperor ordered Xu Chengbai to ride post-haste to treat him.

sentences.zh: 差，成伯還。

translations.literal: When he recovered, Chengbai returned.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered, Chengbai returned.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿定名醫。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You are truly a famous physician."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are truly a famous physician."

sentences.zh: 」賚絹三千疋。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 成伯辭，請受一千。

translations.literal: Chengbai declined and asked to accept only one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbai declined and asked to accept only one thousand.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「《詩》云：'人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Odes says: 'When men of worth perish, the state is laid waste.'"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Odes says: 'When men of worth perish, the state is laid waste.'"

sentences.zh: '以是而言，豈惟三千疋乎？

translations.literal: By that reckoning, is three thousand bolts the limit?
translations.idiomatic: By that reckoning, is three thousand bolts the limit?

sentences.zh: 」其為帝所重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.

sentences.zh: 後所生母雷氏卒，表請解州。

translations.literal: Later his birth mother Lady Lei died; he memorialized asking to resign the province.
translations.idiomatic: Later his birth mother, Lady Lei, died; he memorialized asking to resign the province.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先君餘尊之所厭，《禮》之明文。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The displeasure felt toward a former ruler's lesser consorts is explicit in the Rites."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: "The displeasure felt toward a former ruler's lesser consorts is explicit in the Rites."

sentences.zh: 季末陵遲，斯典或廢。

translations.literal: In the decline of the age that canon has sometimes fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: In the decline of the age that canon has sometimes fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 侯既親王之子，宜從餘尊之義，便可大功。

translations.literal: As the son of an imperial prince you should follow the rule of lesser consorts and may observe the greater mourning.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of an imperial prince you should follow the rule of lesser consorts and may observe the greater mourning.

sentences.zh: 」後卒于雍州刺史，諡曰康侯。

translations.literal: Later he died as governor of Yongzhou; posthumous title Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died in office as governor of Yongzhou and was given the posthumous title Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 衍性清慎，所在廉潔，又不營產業，曆牧四州，皆有稱績，亡日無斂屍具。

translations.literal: Yan was by nature cautious and pure; wherever he served he was incorrupt, kept no estates, and through four provinces left a name for achievement—yet on the day he died there was not even a shroud for his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was by nature cautious and pure. Wherever he served he was incorrupt, kept no estates, and through four provinces left a name for achievement—yet on the day he died there was not even a shroud for his corpse.

sentences.zh: 子暢，字叔暢，從孝武帝入關，拜鴻臚，封博陵王。

translations.literal: His son Chang, styled Shuchang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed Prince of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang, styled Shuchang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed as Prince of Boling.

sentences.zh: 大統三年東討，沒於陣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong he campaigned east and fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he campaigned east and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子敏，嗜酒多費，家為之貧。

translations.literal: His son Min was addicted to wine and extravagant spending; the household was ruined by it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min was addicted to wine and extravagant spending; the household was ruined by it.

sentences.zh: 其婿柱國乙弗貴、大將軍大利稽祐家貲皆千萬，每營給之。

translations.literal: His sons-in-law, pillar of state Yifu Gui and great general Dali Ji You, each had wealth in the tens of millions and supplied him whenever he asked.
translations.idiomatic: His sons-in-law, the pillar of state Yifu Gui and the great general Dali Ji You, each had wealth in the tens of millions and supplied him whenever he asked.

sentences.zh: 敏隨即散盡，而帝不之責。

translations.literal: Min would scatter it all at once, yet the emperor did not reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Min would scatter it all at once, yet the emperor did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 貴、祐後遂絕之。

translations.literal: Gui and You eventually cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and You eventually cut him off.

sentences.zh: 位儀同三司，改封南武縣公。

translations.literal: He held the rank Pillar of State, third grade; his fief was changed to Duke of Nanwu County.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Pillar of State, third grade; his fief was changed to Duke of Nanwu County.

sentences.zh: 暢弟融，字叔融，貌甚短陋，驍武過人。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Rong, styled Shurong, was very short and ugly in appearance yet surpassingly fierce in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Rong, styled Shurong, was very short and ugly in appearance yet surpassingly fierce in battle.

sentences.zh: 莊帝謀殺爾硃榮，以融為直閣將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi plotted to kill Erzhu Rong, Rong was made a direct-gate general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi plotted to kill Erzhu Rong, Rong was made a direct-gate general.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃兆入洛，融逃人間。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Rong fled among the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Rong fled among the people.

sentences.zh: 後從孝武入關，封魏興王，位侍郎、殿中尚書。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, was enfeoffed Prince of Weixing, and held the posts of Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, was enfeoffed Prince of Weixing, and held the posts of Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 衍弟欽，字思若，位中書監、尚書右僕射、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Qin, styled Siruo, held the posts of Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Pillar of State, third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Qin, styled Siruo, held the posts of Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Pillar of State, third grade.

sentences.zh: 欽色尤黑，故時人號為黑面僕射。

translations.literal: Qin's complexion was especially dark, so people of the time called him the Black-Faced Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's complexion was especially dark, so people of the time called him the Black-Faced Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 欽淫從兄麗妻崔氏，為御史中尉封回劾奏，遇赦免。

translations.literal: Qin debauched his cousin Li's wife, the Lady Cui; Censor-in-Chief Feng Hui impeached him, but he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin debauched his cousin Li's wife, the Lady Cui; the censor-in-chief Feng Hui impeached him, but he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋除司州牧。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 欽少好學，早有令譽。

translations.literal: Qin loved learning from youth and had an early reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Qin loved learning from youth and had an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「皇宗略略，壽安、思若。

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Among the imperial clan, briefly—Shou'an and Siruo."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said: "Among the imperial clan, briefly—Shou'an and Siruo."

sentences.zh: 」及晚年貴重，不能有所匡益，論者輕之。

translations.literal: When in later years he grew eminent he could no longer offer useful counsel; critics looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: When in later years he grew eminent he could no longer offer useful counsel; critics looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 欽曾托青州人高僧壽為子求師，師至，未幾逃去。

translations.literal: Qin once asked the man of Qingzhou, the monk Gaosengshou, to find a tutor for his son; the tutor arrived but fled after only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once asked the man of Qingzhou, the monk Gaosengshou, to find a tutor for his son; the tutor arrived but fled after only a few days.

sentences.zh: 欽以讓僧壽。

translations.literal: Qin reproached Gaosengshou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin reproached Gaosengshou.

sentences.zh: 僧壽性滑稽，反謂欽曰：「凡人絕粒七日乃死，始經五朝，便爾逃遁，去食就信，實有所闕。

translations.literal: Gaosengshou, a man of wit, retorted to Qin: "An ordinary man dies after seven days without grain; this one lasted barely five mornings before fleeing—abandoning food for faith, he plainly lacked something."
translations.idiomatic: Gaosengshou, a man of wit, retorted to Qin: "An ordinary man dies after seven days without grain; this one lasted barely five mornings before fleeing—abandoning food for faith, he plainly lacked something."

sentences.zh: 」欽乃大慚，於是待客稍厚。

translations.literal: Qin was deeply ashamed and thereafter treated guests somewhat more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was deeply ashamed and thereafter treated guests somewhat more generously.

sentences.zh: 後除司空公，封钜平縣公。

translations.literal: Later he was made Duke of the State and enfeoffed Duke of Juping County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Duke of the State and enfeoffed as Duke of Juping County.

sentences.zh: 于河陰遇害，贈假黃鉞、太師、太尉公。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin and posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke.

sentences.zh: 子子孝，字季業，早有令譽。

translations.literal: His son Zixiao, styled Jiye, had an early reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zixiao, styled Jiye, had an early reputation.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，司徒崔光見而異之，曰：「後生領袖，必此人也。

translations.literal: At eight years old, Director of the Secretariat Cui Guang saw him and marveled, saying: "The leader of the coming generation will surely be this boy."
translations.idiomatic: At eight years old, Director of the Secretariat Cui Guang saw him and marveled, saying: "The leader of the coming generation will surely be this boy."

sentences.zh: 」孝武帝入關，不及從駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong he did not manage to follow the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong he did not manage to follow the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 後赴長安，封義陽王。

translations.literal: Later he went to Chang'an and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went to Chang'an and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 子孝美容儀，善笑謔，好酒愛士，縉紳歸之，賓客常滿，終日無倦。

translations.literal: Zixiao was handsome, skilled at jest and banter, loved wine and honored scholars; the gentry flocked to him, his hall always full of guests, and he never tired of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiao was handsome, skilled at jest and banter, loved wine and honored scholars; the gentry flocked to him, his hall always full of guests, and he never tired of it.

sentences.zh: 性又寬慈，敦穆親族。

translations.literal: His nature was also generous and kind; he treated his kinsmen with warmth and respect.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also generous and kind; he treated his kinsmen with warmth and respect.

sentences.zh: 乃置學館於私第，集群從子弟，書夜講讀。

translations.literal: He established a school in his private residence and gathered younger kinsmen to lecture day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He established a school in his private residence and gathered younger kinsmen to lecture day and night.

sentences.zh: 並給衣食，與諸子同。

translations.literal: He provided food and clothing and treated them as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: He provided food and clothing and treated them as his own sons.

sentences.zh: 後曆尚書令、柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat and Pillar of State, great general.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat and as Pillar of State, great general.

sentences.zh: 子孝以國運漸移，深自貶晦，日夜縱酒。

translations.literal: Zixiao saw the dynasty's fortune slipping away and humbled himself deeply, drinking day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiao saw the dynasty's fortune slipping away and humbled himself deeply, drinking day and night.

sentences.zh: 後例降為公，復姓拓拔氏。

translations.literal: Later by precedent he was reduced to duke and restored the surname Tuoba.
translations.idiomatic: Later by precedent he was reduced to duke and restored the surname Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，子贇襲。

translations.literal: Before long he died; his son Yun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; his son Yun succeeded.

sentences.zh: 子太興襲，拜長安鎮大將。

translations.literal: Yun's son Taixing succeeded and was made General of Chang'an Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Taixing succeeded and was made General of Chang'an Garrison.

sentences.zh: 以黷貨削除官爵。

translations.literal: For corruption he was stripped of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: For corruption he was stripped of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 後除秘書監，還復前爵，改封西河。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former title, and his fief changed to Xihé.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former title, and his fief changed to Xihé.

sentences.zh: 轉守衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 初，太興遇患，請諸沙門行道。

translations.literal: At first, when Taixing fell ill, he asked monks to perform rites for him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Taixing fell ill, he asked monks to perform rites for him.

sentences.zh: 所有資財，一時佈施，乞求病癒，名曰散生齋。

translations.literal: All his possessions were given away at once in a distribution called the Liberation Fast, begging recovery from illness.
translations.idiomatic: All his possessions were given away at once in a distribution called the Liberation Fast, begging recovery from illness.

sentences.zh: 及齋後，僧皆四散，有一沙門方雲乞齋餘食。

translations.literal: After the fast the monks scattered in all directions; one monk was still asking for leftover food from the fast.
translations.idiomatic: After the fast the monks scattered in all directions; one monk was still asking for leftover food from the fast.

sentences.zh: 太興戲之曰；

translations.literal: Taixing jested with him:
translations.idiomatic: Taixing jested with him:

sentences.zh: 「齋食既盡，唯有酒肉。

translations.literal: "The fast food is gone; only wine and meat remain."
translations.idiomatic: "The fast food is gone; only wine and meat remain."

sentences.zh: 」沙門曰：「亦能食之。

translations.literal: The monk said: "I can eat those too."
translations.idiomatic: The monk said: "I can eat those too."

sentences.zh: 」因出酒一斗，羊腳一隻。

translations.literal: So he brought out a dou of wine and a leg of mutton.
translations.idiomatic: So he brought out a dou of wine and a leg of mutton.

sentences.zh: 食盡，猶言不飽。

translations.literal: When he had finished eating he still said he was not full.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished eating he still said he was not full.

sentences.zh: 及辭出後，酒肉俱在。

translations.literal: After he left, the wine and meat were still there.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, the wine and meat were still there.

sentences.zh: 出門追之，無所見。

translations.literal: Going out the gate to pursue him, he was nowhere to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Going out the gate to pursue him, he was nowhere to be seen.

sentences.zh: 太興遂佛前乞願：「向者之師，當非俗人。

translations.literal: Taixing then prayed before the Buddha: "The master just now must not have been an ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing then prayed before the Buddha: "The master just now must not have been an ordinary man.

sentences.zh: 若此病得差，即舍王爵入道。

translations.literal: If this illness is cured, I will renounce my princely rank and enter the Way."
translations.idiomatic: If this illness is cured, I will renounce my princely rank and enter the Way."

sentences.zh: 」未幾便愈，遂請為沙門。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered and asked to become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he recovered and asked to become a monk.

sentences.zh: 表十餘上，乃見許。

translations.literal: He submitted more than ten memorials before permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten memorials before permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 時孝文南討在軍，詔皇太子于四月八日為之下發，施帛二千疋。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was on the southern campaign with the army; an edict ordered the crown prince on the eighth day of the fourth month to tonsure him and grant two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xiaowen was on the southern campaign with the army. An edict ordered the crown prince on the eighth day of the fourth month to tonsure him and grant two thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 既為沙門，名僧懿，居嵩山。

translations.literal: Having become a monk he took the name Sengyi and dwelt on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Having become a monk he took the name Sengyi and dwelt on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 太和二十二年終。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Taihe he died.

sentences.zh: 子昴，字伯暉，襲，薨。

translations.literal: His son Mao, styled Bohui, succeeded and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao, styled Bohui, succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 昴子忄妻，字魏慶，襲。

translations.literal: Mao's son Cong, styled Weiqing, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's son Cong, styled Weiqing, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，累遷太尉、錄尚書事、司州牧、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaojing he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Commandant, recorded affairs of the Secretariat, governor of Sizhou, and governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaojing he rose to Grand Commandant, recorded affairs of the Secretariat, governor of Sizhou, and governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 薨於州，贈假黃鉞、太傅、司徒公，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Tutor, and Grand Duke; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the province and was posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Tutor, and Grand Duke, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 悰寬和有度量，美容貌，風望儼然。

translations.literal: Cong was generous and measured, handsome in appearance, and carried himself with dignified bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was generous and measured, handsome in appearance, and carried himself with dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 得喪之間，不見於色。

translations.literal: Between gain and loss he showed nothing on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Between gain and loss he showed nothing on his face.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，不營產業，身死之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and frugal; he kept no estates, and on the day he died the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was pure and frugal; he kept no estates, and on the day he died the household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 昴弟仲景，性嚴峭。

translations.literal: Mao's younger brother Zhongjing was by nature stern and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's younger brother Zhongjing was by nature stern and harsh.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，兼御史中尉，京師肅然。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he concurrently served as censor-in-chief; the capital grew orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang he concurrently served as censor-in-chief; the capital grew orderly.

sentences.zh: 每向台，恆駕赤牛，時人號「赤牛中尉」。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to the bureau he always drove a red ox; people of the time called him the Red-Ox Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went to the bureau he always drove a red ox; people of the time called him the Red-Ox Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，為河南尹，奉法無私。

translations.literal: At the start of Taichang he was made governor of Henan and enforced the law without favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taichang he was made governor of Henan and enforced the law without favor.

sentences.zh: 時吏部尚書樊子鵠部下縱橫，又為盜竊。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Fan Zihe's subordinates ran rampant and also committed theft.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the director of the Ministry of Personnel, Fan Zihe, had subordinates who ran rampant and also committed theft.

sentences.zh: 仲景密加收捕，悉獲之，咸即行決。

translations.literal: Zhongjing secretly sent men to arrest them; all were seized and immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing secretly sent men to arrest them; all were seized and immediately executed.

sentences.zh: 於是豪貴寒心。

translations.literal: Thereupon the powerful grew fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the powerful grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝將入關，授仲景中軍大都督，留京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was about to enter Guanzhong, Zhongjing was made commander-in-chief of the central army and left in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu was about to enter Guanzhong, Zhongjing was made commander-in-chief of the central army and left in the capital.

sentences.zh: 齊神武欲至洛陽，仲景遂棄妻子，追駕至長安。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Shenwu was about to reach Luoyang, Zhongjing abandoned wife and children and pursued the imperial carriage to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qi Shenwu was about to reach Luoyang, Zhongjing abandoned wife and children and pursued the imperial carriage to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仍除尚書右僕射，封順陽王。

translations.literal: He was then made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Prince of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Prince of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 仲景既失妻子，乃娶故爾硃天光妻也列氏。

translations.literal: Zhongjing having lost his wife, he married Yelie, the former wife of Erzhu Tianguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing having lost his wife, he married Yelie, the former wife of Erzhu Tianguang.

sentences.zh: 本倡女，有美色，仲景甚重之。

translations.literal: She had been a singing girl, very beautiful; Zhongjing cherished her greatly.
translations.idiomatic: She had been a singing girl, very beautiful; Zhongjing cherished her greatly.

sentences.zh: 經數年，前妻叔袁紇氏自洛陽間行至。

translations.literal: After several years his former wife's uncle, the Lady Yuan He, came secretly from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After several years his former wife's uncle, the Lady Yuan He, came secretly from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 也列遂徙居異宅。

translations.literal: Yelie then moved to a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yelie then moved to a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 久之，有奸。

translations.literal: After a long while there was an affair.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while there was an affair.

sentences.zh: 事露，詔仲景殺之。

translations.literal: When it came to light, an edict ordered Zhongjing to kill her.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to light, an edict ordered Zhongjing to kill her.

sentences.zh: 仲景寵情愈至，謬殺一婢，蒙其屍而厚葬以代焉。

translations.literal: Zhongjing's passion only grew; he falsely killed a maid, wrapped her corpse, and gave her a lavish burial in Yelie's place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing's passion only grew; he falsely killed a maid, wrapped her corpse, and gave her a lavish burial in Yelie's place.

sentences.zh: 列徙於密處，人莫知其詐。

translations.literal: Yelie was hidden in a secret place; no one knew the deception.
translations.idiomatic: Yelie was hidden in a secret place; no one knew the deception.

sentences.zh: 仲景三子濟、鐘、奉，叔袁紇氏生也，皆以宗室，早曆清官。

translations.literal: Zhongjing's three sons Ji, Zhong, and Feng were born to the Lady Yuan He; as members of the imperial clan they early held pure offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing's three sons Ji, Zhong, and Feng were born to the Lady Yuan He; as members of the imperial clan they early held pure offices.

sentences.zh: 仲景以列尚在，恐妻子漏之，乃謀殺袁紇。

translations.literal: Zhongjing, since Yelie was still alive, feared his wife and children might leak the secret and plotted to kill Yuan He.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing, since Yelie was still alive, feared his wife and children might leak the secret and plotted to kill Yuan He.

sentences.zh: 紇先覺，復欲陰害列。

translations.literal: Yuan He sensed it first and in turn plotted to harm Yelie secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan He sensed it first and in turn plotted to harm Yelie secretly.

sentences.zh: 列謂從奴曰：「若袁紇殺我，必投我廁中；

translations.literal: Yelie told her attendant: "If Yuan He kills me, she will surely throw me in the privy;
translations.idiomatic: Yelie told her attendant: "If Yuan He kills me, she will surely throw me in the privy;

sentences.zh: 我告丞相，冀或不死。

translations.literal: I will tell the prime minister and hope I may not die.
translations.idiomatic: I will tell the prime minister and hope I may not die.

sentences.zh: 若不理首愆，猶埋我好地，爾為我告之。

translations.literal: If she does not report the first fault, she may still bury me in good ground—you must tell him for me."
translations.idiomatic: If she does not report the first fault, she may still bury me in good ground—you must tell him for me."

sentences.zh: 」奴遂告周文帝。

translations.literal: The servant then reported to Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The servant then reported to Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周文依奏，詔笞仲景一百，免右僕射，以王歸第。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen acted on the report; an edict ordered a hundred strokes with the rod for Zhongjing, removed him as Right Vice Director, and sent the prince home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen acted on the report. An edict ordered a hundred strokes with the rod for Zhongjing, removed him as Right Vice Director, and sent the prince home.

sentences.zh: 也列以自告而逐之。

translations.literal: Yelie was driven out for having reported the matter herself.
translations.idiomatic: Yelie was driven out for having reported the matter herself.

sentences.zh: 仲景猶私不已。

translations.literal: Zhongjing still kept in contact secretly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing still kept in contact secretly.

sentences.zh: 又有告者，詔重笞一百，付宗正，官爵盡除。

translations.literal: When there was another report, an edict ordered another hundred strokes, handed him to the Director of the Imperial Clan, and stripped him of all office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: When there was another report, an edict ordered another hundred strokes, handed him to the Director of the Imperial Clan, and stripped him of all office and rank.

sentences.zh: 仲景仍通焉。

translations.literal: Zhongjing still kept the liaison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing still kept the liaison.

sentences.zh: 後周文帝以其歷任有令名，且杖策追駕，乃奏復官爵。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Wen of Zhou, because he had held office with a good name and had whipped his horse to pursue the imperial carriage, memorialized to restore his office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wen of Zhou, because he had held office with a good name and had whipped his horse to pursue the imperial carriage, memorialized to restore his office and rank.

sentences.zh: 也列、袁紇於是同居。

translations.literal: Yelie and Yuan He then lived together again.
translations.idiomatic: Yelie and Yuan He then lived together again.

sentences.zh: 大統五年，除幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was made governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was made governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲景多內亂，後就州賜死。

translations.literal: Zhongjing had many domestic disorders; later he was ordered to die at his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing had many domestic disorders; later he was ordered to die at his post.

sentences.zh: 太興弟遙，字太原，有器望。

translations.literal: Taixing's younger brother Yao, styled Taiyuan, had ability and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Taixing's younger brother Yao, styled Taiyuan, had ability and reputation.

sentences.zh: 以左衛將軍從孝文南征，賜爵饒陽男。

translations.literal: As General of the Left Guard he followed Emperor Xiaowen on the southern campaign and was granted the title Baron of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: As General of the Left Guard he followed Emperor Xiaowen on the southern campaign and was granted the title Baron of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，遭所生母憂，表請解任。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was struck by his birth mother's death and memorialized asking to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was struck by his birth mother's death and memorialized asking to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 詔以餘尊所厭，不許。

translations.literal: An edict said that the displeasure toward a former ruler's lesser consorts did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said that the displeasure toward a former ruler's lesser consorts did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，累遷左光祿大夫，仍領護軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace and still commanded the guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he was repeatedly promoted to Left Grand Master of the Palace and still commanded the guard.

sentences.zh: 時冀州沙門法慶既為妖幻，遂說勃海人李歸伯。

translations.literal: At the time the monk Faqing of Jizhou had wrought demonic illusions and persuaded Li Guibo of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the monk Faqing of Jizhou had wrought demonic illusions and persuaded Li Guibo of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 歸伯闔家從之，招率鄉人，推法慶為主。

translations.literal: Guibo's whole household followed him; he rallied the countryside and set up Faqing as leader.
translations.idiomatic: Guibo's whole household followed him; he rallied the countryside and set up Faqing as leader.

sentences.zh: 法慶以歸伯為十住菩薩、平魔軍司、定漢王，自號大乘。

translations.literal: Faqing made Guibo the Ten-Abode Bodhisattva, Marshal Who Pacifies Demons, and King Who Settles Han; he styled himself Mahayana.
translations.idiomatic: Faqing made Guibo the Ten-Abode Bodhisattva, Marshal Who Pacifies Demons, and King Who Settles Han; he styled himself Mahayana.

sentences.zh: 殺一人者為一住菩薩，殺十人者為十住菩薩。

translations.literal: Whoever killed one person was a one-abode bodhisattva; whoever killed ten was a ten-abode bodhisattva.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever killed one person was a one-abode bodhisattva; whoever killed ten was a ten-abode bodhisattva.

sentences.zh: 又合狂藥，令人服之，父子兄弟不相知識，唯以殺害為事。

translations.literal: He also mixed mad drugs; whoever took them lost knowledge of father, brother, or son and knew only killing.
translations.idiomatic: He also mixed mad drugs; whoever took them lost knowledge of father, brother, or son and knew only killing.

sentences.zh: 刺史蕭寶夤遣兼長史崔伯驎討之，敗於煮棗城，伯驎戰沒。

translations.literal: Governor Xiao Baoyin sent his acting chief clerk Cui Bolin to attack them; he was defeated at Zhuzao City and Bolin died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Xiao Baoyin sent his acting chief clerk Cui Bolin to attack them; he was defeated at Zhuzao City and Bolin died in battle.

sentences.zh: 凶眾遂盛，所在屠滅寺舍，斬戮僧尼，焚燒經像，云：「新佛出世，除去眾魔。

translations.literal: The rebels grew mighty; wherever they went they slaughtered monasteries, cut down monks and nuns, burned sutras and images, saying: "The new Buddha has appeared to remove the demons."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels grew mighty; wherever they went they slaughtered monasteries, cut down monks and nuns, burned sutras and images, saying: "The new Buddha has appeared to remove the demons."

sentences.zh: 」詔以遙為使持節、都督北征諸軍事，討破之。

translations.literal: An edict made Yao bearer of the staff of authority and commander of the northern expedition; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yao bearer of the staff of authority and commander of the northern expedition; he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 禽法慶，並其妻尼惠暉等。

translations.literal: He captured Faqing together with his wife the nun Huihui and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Faqing together with his wife the nun Huihui and the rest.

sentences.zh: 斬法慶，傳首京師；

translations.literal: Faqing was beheaded and his head sent to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Faqing was beheaded and his head sent to the capital;

sentences.zh: 後禽歸伯，戮于都市。

translations.literal: later Guibo was captured and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: later Guibo was captured and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 初，遙大功昆弟皆是景穆之孫，至明帝而本服絕，故除遙等屬籍。

translations.literal: At first Yao's elder cousins in the greater mourning line were all grandsons of Jingmu; by Emperor Ming's time the primary mourning bond was exhausted, so Yao and the rest were removed from the imperial register.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yao's elder cousins in the greater mourning line were all grandsons of Jingmu; by Emperor Ming's time the primary mourning bond was exhausted, so Yao and the rest were removed from the imperial register.

sentences.zh: 遙表曰：

translations.literal: Yao memorialized:
translations.idiomatic: Yao memorialized:

sentences.zh: 竊聞聖人所以南面而聽天下，其不可得變革者，則親也尊也。

translations.literal: I have heard that the reason the sage faces south and listens to all under Heaven is that among what cannot be altered are kinship and honor.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the reason the sage faces south and listens to all under Heaven is that among what cannot be altered are kinship and honor.

sentences.zh: 四世而緦服窮，五世而袒免，六世而親屬竭矣。

translations.literal: After four generations the finest mourning ends; after five, the bared shoulder; after six, kinship is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After four generations the finest mourning ends; after five, the bared shoulder; after six, kinship is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 去茲以往，猶系之以姓而弗別，綴之以食而弗殊。

translations.literal: Beyond that, kin are still linked by surname without division, joined by sacrificial food without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond that, kin are still linked by surname without division, joined by sacrificial food without distinction.

sentences.zh: 又《律》雲議親者，非唯當世之屬親，曆謂先帝之五世。

translations.literal: The Code also says that those debated as kin are not only kin of the present generation but extend to the former emperor's five generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Code also says that those debated as kin are not only kin of the present generation but extend to the former emperor's five generations.

sentences.zh: 謹尋斯旨，將以廣帝宗，重磐石。

translations.literal: Examining this intent, it is meant to broaden the imperial clan and strengthen the bedrock.
translations.idiomatic: Examining this intent, it is meant to broaden the imperial clan and strengthen the bedrock.

sentences.zh: 先皇所以變茲事條，為此別制者，太和之季，方有意于吳、蜀；

translations.literal: The reason the late emperor altered this statute and made this separate rule was that in the Taihe years he still had designs on Wu and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: The reason the late emperor altered this statute and made this separate rule was that in the Taihe years he still had designs on Wu and Shu;

sentences.zh: 經始之費，慮深在初；

translations.literal: the cost of beginning the enterprise lay deep in the outset;
translations.idiomatic: the cost of beginning the enterprise lay deep in the outset;

sentences.zh: 割減之起，暫出當時也。

translations.literal: the reduction arose temporarily from that moment.
translations.idiomatic: the reduction arose temporarily from that moment.

sentences.zh: 且臨淮王提分屬籍之始，高祖賜帛三千疋，所以重分離。

translations.literal: Moreover when Prince of Huaiyang Ti was first removed from the register, the High Ancestor granted three thousand bolts of silk to emphasize the separation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when the Prince of Huaiyang, Ti, was first removed from the register, the High Ancestor granted three thousand bolts of silk to emphasize the separation.

sentences.zh: 樂良王長命亦賜縑二千疋，所以存慈眷。

translations.literal: Prince of Leliang Changming also received two thousand bolts of silk to preserve affectionate regard.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Leliang, Changming, also received two thousand bolts of silk to preserve affectionate regard.

sentences.zh: 此皆先朝殷勤克念，不得已而然者也。

translations.literal: These were all the former court's earnest, thoughtful remembrance—done because there was no other way.
translations.idiomatic: These were all the former court's earnest, thoughtful remembrance—done because there was no other way.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，「百足之蟲，至死不僵」者，以其輔己者眾。

translations.literal: The ancients said, "A centipede does not stiffen until death" because those who support it are many.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "A centipede does not stiffen until death" because those who support it are many.

sentences.zh: 臣誠不欲妄親太階，苟求潤屋，但傷大宗一分，則天子屬籍不過十數人而已。

translations.literal: I truly do not wish rashly to approach the Great Steps or seek to enrich my house, but it grieves me that with one portion cut from the great lineage the emperor's register holds barely a dozen names.
translations.idiomatic: I truly do not wish rashly to approach the Great Steps or seek to enrich my house, but it grieves me that with one portion cut from the great lineage the emperor's register holds barely a dozen names.

sentences.zh: 在漢諸王之子，不限多少，皆列土而封，謂之曰侯；

translations.literal: Under Han, the sons of the kings, without limit on number, all received fiefs and were called marquises;
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, the sons of the kings, without limit on number, all received fiefs and were called marquises;

sentences.zh: 至於魏、晉，莫不廣胙河山，稱之曰公者，蓋惡其大宗之不固，骨肉之恩疏矣。

translations.literal: down through Wei and Jin none failed to grant broad fiefs across rivers and mountains and call them dukes—because they hated that the great lineage was not firm and flesh-and-blood affection grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: down through Wei and Jin none failed to grant broad fiefs across rivers and mountains and call them dukes—because they hated that the great lineage was not firm and flesh-and-blood affection grew thin.

sentences.zh: 臣去皇上雖是五世之遠，於先帝便是天子之孫。

translations.literal: Though I am five generations removed from Your Majesty, to the late emperor I was still the emperor's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am five generations removed from Your Majesty, to the late emperor I was still the emperor's grandson.

sentences.zh: 高祖所以國秩祿賦，復給衣食，後族唯給其賦，不與衣食者，欲以別外內，限異同也。

translations.literal: The reason the High Ancestor restored state stipends and grain levies and again gave food and clothing, while the empress's kin received only the levy and not food or clothing, was to distinguish inner from outer and set limits on sameness and difference.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the High Ancestor restored state stipends and grain levies and again gave food and clothing, while the empress's kin received only the levy and not food or clothing, was to distinguish inner from outer and set limits on sameness and difference.

sentences.zh: 今諸廟之感，在心未忘；

translations.literal: The feeling owed the ancestral temples is not yet forgotten in the heart;
translations.idiomatic: The feeling owed the ancestral temples is not yet forgotten in the heart;

sentences.zh: 行道之悲，倏然已及。

translations.literal: the grief of the road has suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: the grief of the road has suddenly arrived.

sentences.zh: 其諸封者，身亡之日，三年服終，然後改奪。

translations.literal: Those enfeoffed, when they die, after three years of mourning the title is then altered or withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Those enfeoffed, when they die, after three years of mourning the title is then altered or withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷猶在遏密之中，便議此事，實用未安。

translations.literal: The court is still in the period of suppressed mourning; to debate this matter now is truly not yet fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The court is still in the period of suppressed mourning; to debate this matter now is truly not yet fitting.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書博議以聞。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the Ministry for broad deliberation and report.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred it to the Ministry for broad deliberation and report.

sentences.zh: 尚書令任城王澄、尚書左僕射元暉奏同遙表，靈太后不從。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Rencheng Cheng and Left Vice Director Yuan Hui memorialized agreement with Yao's memorial; Empress Dowager Ling did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Prince of Rencheng Cheng and Left Vice Director Yuan Hui memorialized agreement with Yao's memorial; Empress Dowager Ling did not follow it.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰宣公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Duke Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Duke Xuan.

sentences.zh: 遙弟恆，字景安，粗涉書史。

translations.literal: Yao's younger brother Heng, styled Jing'an, had a rough acquaintance with books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's younger brother Heng, styled Jing'an, had a rough acquaintance with books and histories.

sentences.zh: 恆以《春秋》之義，為名不以山川，表求改名芝。

translations.literal: Heng, following the Spring and Autumn principle that names do not take mountains and rivers, memorialized asking to change his name to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, following the Spring and Autumn principle that names do not take mountains and rivers, memorialized asking to change his name to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 歷位太常卿、中書監、侍中。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Director of the Court of Sacrifices, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of Director of the Court of Sacrifices, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後於河陰遇害，贈太傅、司徒公，諡曰宣穆公。

translations.literal: Later he was killed at Heyin; posthumously given Grand Tutor and Grand Duke; posthumous title Duke Xuanmu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was killed at Heyin and posthumously given Grand Tutor and Grand Duke, with the posthumous title Duke Xuanmu.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王小新成，和平二年封，頗有武略。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng, was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping and had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng, was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping and had considerable military talent.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚侵擾，詔新成討之。

translations.literal: When the Kumo Xi raided, an edict ordered Xiaoxincheng to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kumo Xi raided, an edict ordered Xiaoxincheng to attack them.

sentences.zh: 新成乃多為毒酒。

translations.literal: Xiaoxincheng prepared much poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxincheng prepared much poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 賊逼，便棄營而去。

translations.literal: When the bandits pressed close he abandoned the camp and left.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits pressed close he abandoned the camp and left.

sentences.zh: 賊至，兢飲。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived they drank eagerly.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits arrived they drank eagerly.

sentences.zh: 遂簡輕騎縱擊，俘馘甚多。

translations.literal: He then led light cavalry in a swift strike and took many captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: He then led light cavalry in a swift strike and took many captives and heads.

sentences.zh: 後位外都大官。

translations.literal: Later he held the office of Grand Official of the Outer Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Grand Official of the Outer Capital.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈大將軍，諡曰惠公。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Grand General; his posthumous title was Duke Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Grand General, with the posthumous title Duke Hui.

sentences.zh: 子鬱，字伏生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yu, courtesy name Fusheng, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu, courtesy name Fusheng, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 位開府，為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He held the rank of Defender-in-Chief and was Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Defender-in-Chief and served as Governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 以黷貨賜死，國除。

translations.literal: For corrupt greed he was granted death; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For corruption he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 長子弼，字邕明，剛正有文學，位中散大夫。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bi, courtesy name Yongming, was upright and possessed literary learning; he held the office of Palace Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Bi, courtesy name Yongming, was upright and literary; he served as Palace Scribe.

sentences.zh: 以世嫡，應襲先爵。

translations.literal: As heir of the main line, he ought to have inherited the former title.
translations.idiomatic: As heir of the main line he should have inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 為季父尚書僕射麗因於氏親寵，遂奪弼王爵，橫授同母兄子誕。

translations.literal: His younger uncle, Minister of the Masters of Writing Lü, because of the Yu clan's favor, then seized Bi's princely rank and arbitrarily granted it to his elder brother's son Dan by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger uncle Lü, Minister of the Masters of Writing, used the Yu clan's favor to strip Bi of his princely rank and give it to his full brother's son Dan.

sentences.zh: 於是弼絕棄人事，托疾還私第。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bi utterly abandoned worldly affairs and pleaded illness to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then withdrew from public life entirely, citing illness to return home.

sentences.zh: 宣武徵為侍中，弼上表固讓。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu summoned him as Palace Attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu summoned him as Palace Attendant, but Bi firmly declined in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 入嵩山，以穴為室，布衣蔬食。

translations.literal: He entered Mount Song, taking a cave for his dwelling, wearing coarse cloth and eating plain food.
translations.idiomatic: He went into Mount Song, made a cave his home, and lived on coarse cloth and plain food.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 建義元年，子暉業訴復王爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyi, his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi his son Huiye petitioned to have the princely rank restored.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，追贈尚書令、司徒公，諡曰「文獻」。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the State of Situ; his posthumous title was "Wenxian."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Situ, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

sentences.zh: 初，弼嘗夢人謂之曰：「君身不得傳世封，其紹先爵者，君長子紹遠也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Bi once dreamed that someone told him: "Your person cannot transmit the hereditary enfeoffment; he who will continue the former title is your eldest son Shaoyuan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bi had dreamed that someone told him, "You yourself will not pass on the hereditary fief; the one who will inherit the former title is your eldest son Shaoyuan."

sentences.zh: 」弼覺，即語暉業，終如其言。

translations.literal: When Bi awoke he at once told Huiye, and in the end it was as the words had said.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi awoke he told Huiye at once, and in the end it proved exactly as the dream had said.

sentences.zh: 暉業少險薄，多與寇盜交通。

translations.literal: Huiye in youth was treacherous and shallow, and often associated with bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Huiye was treacherous and dissolute and often consorted with bandits.

sentences.zh: 長乃變節，涉子史，亦頗屬文，而慷慨有志節。

translations.literal: When grown he changed his ways, studied histories and annals, and also wrote rather well, yet was generous and possessed resolve.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he reformed, studied history, wrote passably well, and became generous and resolute.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太尉，加特進，領中書監，錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He successively held the offices of Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, with special advancement, and concurrently Director of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Minister of Works and Grand Commandant to special advancement, and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄嘗問之曰：「比何所披覽？

translations.literal: Qi Prince Wenxiang once asked him: "What have you been reading lately?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi once asked him, "What have you been reading lately?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「數尋伊、霍之傳，不讀曹、馬之書。

translations.literal: He replied: "I often seek the traditions of Yi and Huo; I do not read the books of Cao and Sima."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I keep to the stories of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao Cao and the Simas."

sentences.zh: 」暉業以時運漸謝，不復圖全。

translations.literal: Huiye, because the times were gradually declining, no longer plotted to preserve himself whole.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the times fade, Huiye no longer strove to preserve himself intact.

sentences.zh: 唯事飲啖，一日三羊，三日一犢。

translations.literal: He devoted himself only to eating and drinking—three sheep in a day, a calf every three days.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself only to feasting—three sheep a day and a calf every three days.

sentences.zh: 又嘗賦詩云：「昔居王道泰，濟濟富群英。

translations.literal: He also once composed a poem saying: "Once I dwelt when the royal way was at peace, / In abundance the host of worthies flourished."
translations.idiomatic: He also once wrote a poem: "Once I lived when the royal way was tranquil, / and hosts of worthies flourished in plenty."

sentences.zh: 今逢世路阻，狐兔鬱縱橫。

translations.literal: "Now I meet the road of the age obstructed, / Foxes and hares throng in every direction."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the age's road is blocked, / and foxes and hares swarm on every side."

sentences.zh: 」齊初，降封美陽縣公，開府儀同三司、特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Meiyang County, Defender-in-Chief with the same ceremony as the Three Dukes, and special advancement.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Qi he was demoted to Duke of Meiyang County while retaining Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke ceremony and special advancement.

sentences.zh: 暉業之在晉陽也，無所交通，居常閒暇，乃撰魏籓王家世，號為《辨宗錄》四十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: While Huiye was at Jinyang he had no social ties; in his usual leisure he compiled the lineages of Wei princely houses, titled Records for Distinguishing Clans in forty scrolls, and it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he kept no company; in his leisure he compiled the genealogies of Wei princely houses into forty scrolls called Records for Distinguishing Clans, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 位望隆重，又以性氣不倫，每被猜忌。

translations.literal: His position and eminence were weighty, and because his temperament was unorthodox he was often suspected.
translations.idiomatic: His rank and standing were great, and because his temperament was eccentric he was often suspected.

sentences.zh: 天保二年，從駕至晉陽，于宮門外罵元韶曰：「爾不及一老嫗，背負璽與人，何不打碎之！

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, following the emperor to Jinyang, outside the palace gate he cursed Yuan Shao, saying: "You are not the equal of an old woman—carrying the seal on your back to hand it to another; why not smash it to pieces!"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao, on the imperial progress to Jinyang, he cursed Yuan Shao outside the palace gate: "You are worse than an old crone, carrying the seal on your back to give it away—why not smash it to bits!"

sentences.zh: 我出此言，知即死，然爾亦詎得幾時！

translations.literal: "I speak these words knowing I shall die at once, yet how much longer can you last!"
translations.idiomatic: "I say this knowing I shall die at once—but how much longer will you last!"

sentences.zh: 」文宣聞而殺之，並斬臨淮公孝友。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan heard and killed him, and also beheaded the Prince of Linhuai, Xiaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan heard of it and had him executed, and also beheaded the Prince of Linhuai, Xiaoyou.

sentences.zh: 孝友臨刑，驚惶失措，暉業神色自若。

translations.literal: At the execution Xiaoyou was panic-stricken and lost composure; Huiye's expression was calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: At the block Xiaoyou was panic-stricken; Huiye's face remained serene.

sentences.zh: 仍鑿冰沈其屍。

translations.literal: They then cut ice and sank their corpses in it.
translations.idiomatic: Their bodies were then sunk in a hole cut through the ice.

sentences.zh: 暉業弟昭業，頗有學尚，位諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was rather learned and held the office of Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was learned and served as Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 莊帝將幸洛南，昭業立於閶闔門外，叩馬諫，帝避之而過。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to visit the south of the Luo, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed through.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to travel south of the Luo, Zhaoye stood outside Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed on.

sentences.zh: 後勞勉之。

translations.literal: Later the emperor praised and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 位給事黃門侍郎、衛將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He held the offices of Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters, Guards General, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters, Guards General, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the right.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文侯。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 郁弟偃，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Yan held the office of Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Yan served as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 子撫，字伯懿，襲。

translations.literal: His son Fu, courtesy name Boyi, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Boyi, inherited.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，為從兄暉業訴奪王爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangzong's reign, on behalf of his cousin Huiye he petitioned to seize back the princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuangzong's reign he petitioned on his cousin Huiye's behalf to recover the princely rank.

sentences.zh: 拜雍州刺史，為政嚴酷，吏人患之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Yong Province; his government was harsh and cruel, and officials and people suffered under it.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Governor of Yong Province, he governed with harsh cruelty that officials and commoners alike resented.

sentences.zh: 其妻崔氏誕一男，麗遂出州獄囚，死及徒、流案未申台者，一時放免。

translations.literal: When his wife the Lady Cui bore a son, Li then released the prisoners in the provincial jail—those condemned to death and those in exile or banishment whose cases had not yet been reported to the central offices—and pardoned them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife Lady Cui bore a son, Li released all prisoners in the provincial jail, including those awaiting execution or exile whose cases had not yet been sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷冀州刺史，入為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Ji Province and entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Ji Province, then entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「聞公在州殺戮無理，枉濫非一，又大殺道人。

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "I hear that in your province you killed without reason, wrongly condemned many, and also massacred a great number of Buddhist clergy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hear that in your province you killed without cause, wronged many unjustly, and slaughtered a great many monks besides."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣在冀州可殺道人二百許人，亦復何多？

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant in Ji Province could kill on the order of two hundred monks—how is that so many?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In Ji Province I might have killed some two hundred monks—is that really so many?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「一物不得其所，若納諸隍，況殺道人二百，而言不多！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If a single creature does not obtain its proper place, it is as though one were casting it into a moat—how much more when two hundred monks were killed, yet you say it is not many!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When even one creature is wronged it is as though cast into a ditch—yet you killed two hundred monks and call that not many!"

sentences.zh: 」麗脫冠謝，賜坐。

translations.literal: Li removed his cap and apologized; he was granted a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Li removed his cap and apologized; the emperor granted him a seat.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰威。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Wei.

sentences.zh: 子顯和，少有節操，曆司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: His son Xianhe in youth possessed moral discipline and successively served as Recorder of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianhe in youth had moral discipline and served as Recorder in the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 司徒崔光每見之，曰：「元參軍風流清秀，容止閒雅，乃宰相之器。

translations.literal: Minister of State Cui Guang whenever he saw him said: "Recorder Yuan is refined and clear in bearing, graceful and leisurely in deportment—the stuff of a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Minister of State Cui Guang saw him he said, "Recorder Yuan is refined and graceful in bearing—the makings of a chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」除徐州安東府長史。

translations.literal: He was made Long History of the Eastern Pacification Office of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Long History of the Eastern Pacification Office in Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史元法僧叛，顯和與戰被禽。

translations.literal: The Governor Yuan Faseng rebelled; Xianhe fought and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Yuan Faseng rebelled, Xianhe fought and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 執手命與連坐。

translations.literal: Faseng took his hand and ordered him to sit together.
translations.idiomatic: Faseng took his hand and ordered him to sit with him.

sentences.zh: 顯和曰：「顯和與阿翁同源別派，皆是磐石之宗，一朝以地外叛，若遇董狐，能無慚德？

translations.literal: Xianhe said: "Xianhe and my elder kinsman share one source but different branches—we are all of the bedrock clan. Yet in a morning you rebel with this territory in hand; if Dong Hu were here, could you be without shame in virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe said, "Your lordship and I spring from one root, though different branches—we are bedrock of the imperial house. Yet in a morning you rebel holding this land; faced with Dong Hu's brush, could you bear no shame?"

sentences.zh: 」遂不肯坐。

translations.literal: He then refused to sit.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to sit.

sentences.zh: 法僧猶欲慰喻。

translations.literal: Faseng still wished to comfort and persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Faseng still tried to comfort and persuade him.

sentences.zh: 顯和曰：「乃可死作惡鬼，不能生為叛臣！

translations.literal: Xianhe said: "I can die and become an evil ghost, but I cannot live and be a rebel minister!"
translations.idiomatic: Xianhe said, "I would rather die and be an evil ghost than live as a rebel minister!"

sentences.zh: 」及將殺之，神色自若。

translations.literal: When they were about to kill him, his expression was calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to execute him, his face remained serene.

sentences.zh: 建義初，贈秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was posthumously made Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was posthumously made Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 汝陰王天賜，和平三年封，後為內都大官。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ruyin, Tian Ci, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and later was Grand Official of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ruyin, Tian Ci, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and later became Grand Official of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，殿中尚書胡莫寒簡西部敕勒豪富兼丁者，為殿中武士，而大納財貨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Palace Attendant of the Hall Hu Mo Han selected the wealthy of the western Tiele tribes who also held military households to serve as palace warriors, while greatly taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Palace Attendant Hu Mo Han drafted wealthy men from the western Tiele who also bore military household status as palace guards, while taking heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 眾怒，殺莫寒及高平假鎮將奚陵。

translations.literal: The masses were enraged and killed Mo Han and the acting commander of Gaoping, Xi Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The people rose in fury and killed Mo Han and the acting commander of Gaoping, Xi Ling.

sentences.zh: 於是諸部敕勒悉叛。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the Tiele tribes rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the Tiele tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔天賜與給事中羅雲討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tian Ci and Attendant of the Masters of Writing Luo Yun to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Tian Ci and Attendant of the Masters of Writing Luo Yun to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 前鋒敕勒詐降，雲信之。

translations.literal: The vanguard Tiele feigned surrender; Yun believed them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele vanguard feigned surrender, and Yun believed them.

sentences.zh: 副將元伏曰：「敕勒色動，恐有變，今不設備，將為所圖。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Yuan Fu said: "The Tiele show shifting color—fear there will be a change; if we do not prepare now, we shall be plotted against."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Yuan Fu said, "The Tiele look restless—there may be treachery; if we do not prepare now we shall be ambushed."

sentences.zh: 」雲不從。

translations.literal: Yun did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yun would not listen.

sentences.zh: 敕勒襲殺雲，天賜僅得自全。

translations.literal: The Tiele attacked and killed Yun; Tian Ci barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele attacked and killed Yun; Tian Ci barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 累遷懷朔鎮大將。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Huaishuo Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Huaishuo Garrison.

sentences.zh: 坐貪殘，恕死，削除官爵。

translations.literal: For greed and cruelty he was pardoned from death but stripped of office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: For greed and cruelty he was spared death but stripped of office and rank.

sentences.zh: 卒，孝文哭於思政觀，贈本爵，葬從王禮，諡曰靈王。

translations.literal: At his death Emperor Xiaowen wept at Sizheng Hall; he was posthumously granted his former title, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous title Prince Ling.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Emperor Xiaowen wept at Sizheng Hall; he was posthumously restored to his former title, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous name Prince Ling.

sentences.zh: 子逞，字萬安，卒于齊州刺史，諡曰威。

translations.literal: His son Cheng, courtesy name Wan'an, died as Governor of Qi Province; his posthumous title was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cheng, courtesy name Wan'an, died as Governor of Qi Province with the posthumous title Wei.

sentences.zh: 逞子慶和，東豫州刺史，為梁將所攻，舉城降之。

translations.literal: Cheng's son Qinghe was Governor of Eastern Yu Province; when attacked by Liang generals he surrendered the city to them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's son Qinghe, Governor of Eastern Yu Province, surrendered his city when Liang generals attacked.

sentences.zh: 梁武以為北道總督、魏王。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang made him Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Route and Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang made him Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Route and Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 至項城，朝廷出師討之，望風退走。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiangcheng the court sent troops to punish him; he fled at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Xiangcheng the court sent troops against him; he fled at the first rumor of their approach.

sentences.zh: 梁武責之曰：「言同百舌，膽若鼷鼠。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang reproached him: "Your words match a hundred tongues, your courage is like a mouse's."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang rebuked him: "Your tongue runs with a hundred voices, your courage is that of a mouse."

sentences.zh: 」遂徙合浦。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: He was then banished to Hepu.

sentences.zh: 逞弟泛，字普安，自元士稍遷營州刺史。

translations.literal: Cheng's younger brother Fan, courtesy name Pu'an, rose from a Yuan clansman of lower rank to Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Fan, courtesy name Pu'an, rose from junior clansman rank to Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 性貪殘，人不堪命，相率逐之，泛走平州。

translations.literal: Greedy and cruel by nature, the people could not endure his rule and together drove him out; Fan fled to Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and cruel, he drove the people past endurance until they expelled him together; Fan fled to Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 後除光祿大夫、宗正卿，封東燕縣男。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Director of the Imperial Clan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dongyan County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed as Baron of Dongyan.

sentences.zh: 于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: He met disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 泛弟修義，字壽安，頗有文才。

translations.literal: Fan's younger brother Xiuyi, courtesy name Shou'an, possessed considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Xiuyi, courtesy name Shou'an, had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 自元士稍遷齊州刺史。

translations.literal: From a Yuan clansman of lower rank he was gradually promoted to Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: From junior clansman rank he was gradually promoted to Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 修義以齊州頻喪刺史，累表固辭。

translations.literal: Xiuyi, because Qi Province had repeatedly lost its governors, submitted many memorials firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qi Province had repeatedly lost its governors, Xiuyi memorialized again and again to decline the post.

sentences.zh: 詔不許，聽隨便立解宇。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it but allowed him to establish his headquarters wherever he wished.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused but allowed him to set up headquarters wherever he chose.

sentences.zh: 修義乃移東城。

translations.literal: Xiuyi then moved to Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi then moved his seat to Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 為政寬和。

translations.literal: His government was lenient and mild.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and mild.

sentences.zh: 遷秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，表陳庶人禧、庶人愉等，請宥前愆，賜葬陵域。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he memorialized concerning the commoners Xi and the commoner Yu, asking pardon for their former faults and burial in the imperial mausoleum domain.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he memorialized on behalf of the demoted princes Xi and Yu, asking pardon for their past faults and burial in the imperial necropolis.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔曰：「收葬之恩，事由上旨，籓岳何得越職幹陳！」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling edicted: "The grace of gathering for burial is a matter of the supreme will—how may a frontier prince overstep his office and interfere with such a presentation!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling edicted, "The grace of burial lies with the throne alone—how may a frontier prince overstep his station and meddle in such a petition!"

sentences.zh: 在州多受納。

translations.literal: In the province he accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he accepted many bribes.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及在銓衡，唯事貨賄，授官大小，皆有定價。

translations.literal: While holding the scales of appointment he dealt only in bribes; large or small office all had fixed prices.
translations.idiomatic: At the helm of appointments he dealt only in bribes; every office had its price.

sentences.zh: 時中散大夫高居者，有旨先敘。

translations.literal: At that time the Palace Scribe Gao Ju had an imperial instruction for prior promotion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Palace Scribe Gao Ju held an imperial instruction for prior promotion.

sentences.zh: 上党郡缺，居遂求之。

translations.literal: The post of Shangdang Commandery was vacant; Ju then sought it.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Shangdang commandery fell vacant, Ju sought it.

sentences.zh: 修義私已許人，仰居不與。

translations.literal: Xiuyi had already privately promised it to another; relying on Ju's status he would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi had already promised it privately to another and, relying on Ju's rank, refused to grant it.

sentences.zh: 居大言不遜，修義命左右牽曳之。

translations.literal: Ju spoke with great insolence; Xiuyi ordered his attendants to drag him along.
