translations.idiomatic: Ju spoke with great insolence; Xiuyi ordered his attendants to drag him off.

sentences.zh: 居對大眾呼天唱賊。

translations.literal: Before the assembled crowd Ju called to Heaven and cried "Thief!"
translations.idiomatic: Before the assembled crowd Ju cried to Heaven, shouting "Thief!"

sentences.zh: 人問居曰：「白日公庭，安得有賊？

translations.literal: Someone asked Ju: "In broad daylight in the public hall, how can there be a thief?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Ju, "In broad daylight in the public hall, how can there be a thief?"

sentences.zh: 」居指修義曰：「此坐上者，違天子明詔，物多者得官，京師白劫，此非大賊乎？

translations.literal: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said: "This one seated above—he violates the Son of Heaven's clear edict; whoever has more goods gets office. Daylight robbery in the capital— is this not a great thief?"
translations.idiomatic: Ju pointed at Xiuyi and said, "The man seated there violates the Son of Heaven's clear edict—whoever brings more goods gets office. Robbery in broad daylight at the capital—is that not the greatest thief of all?"

sentences.zh: 」修義失色。

translations.literal: Xiuyi turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi turned pale.

sentences.zh: 居行罵而出，後欲邀車駕論修義罪狀，左僕射蕭寶夤喻之乃止。

translations.literal: Ju went out cursing; later he wished to intercept the imperial carriage to argue Xiuyi's crimes, but Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin persuaded him and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ju stormed out still cursing; later he meant to waylay the imperial carriage to denounce Xiuyi's crimes, but Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin talked him out of it.

sentences.zh: 二秦反，假修義兼尚書右僕射、西道行台、行秦州事，為諸軍節度。

translations.literal: When the two Qins rebelled, Xiuyi was provisionally made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Western Route Commissioner, and acting Governor of Qin Province, commanding all armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the two Qin provinces rebelled, Xiuyi was made acting Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Western Route Commissioner, and acting Governor of Qin, with command over all forces.

sentences.zh: 修義性好酒，每飲連日，遂遇風病，神明昏喪，雖至長安，竟無部分之益。

translations.literal: Xiuyi by nature loved wine; each bout of drinking lasted many days, and he then met wind illness—his spirit dim and lost—so that though he reached Chang'an he ultimately brought no benefit of disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi loved wine; each bout lasted days on end until wind illness struck and his mind grew clouded, so that though he reached Chang'an he could offer no effective command.

sentences.zh: 元志敗沒，賊東至黑水，更遣蕭寶夤討之，以修義為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhi was defeated and perished; the rebels advanced east to Heishui; they again sent Xiao Baoyin to campaign, with Xiuyi as Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhi was defeated and killed the rebels advanced east to Heishui; Xiao Baoyin was again sent against them, with Xiuyi as Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 卒于州，贈司空，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumously made Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子均，位給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Jun held the office of Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters.

sentences.zh: 後入西魏，封安昌王，位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he entered Western Wei, was enfeoffed Prince of Anchang, and held the rank of Defender-in-Chief with the same ceremony as the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered Western Wei, was enfeoffed Prince of Anchang, and held Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke ceremony.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈司空，諡曰平。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Ping.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Ping.

sentences.zh: 子則，字孝規，襲爵，位義州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Ze, courtesy name Xiaogui, inherited the title and held the office of Governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze, courtesy name Xiaogui, inherited the title and served as Governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 仕周為小塚宰、江陵總管。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou he was Junior Director of the Mausoleum and Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Junior Director of the Mausoleum and Commander-in-Chief of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 既而宇文化及立秦王浩為帝，擁兵至彭城，所在響震。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Yuwen Huaji established the Prince of Qin Hao as emperor and led troops to Pengcheng; wherever he passed the land trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuwen Huaji set up Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and marched to Pengcheng; the land shook wherever his army passed.

sentences.zh: 文都諷侗遣使通于李密。

translations.literal: Wendu persuaded Tong to send envoys to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu persuaded Yang Tong to send envoys to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密乃請降，因授官爵，禮其使甚厚。

translations.literal: Mi then requested surrender and was thereupon granted office and rank; Tong treated his envoys with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi then offered to submit and was granted office and rank; Tong treated his envoys with great honor.

sentences.zh: 王世充不悅，文都知之，陰有誅世充計。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong was displeased; Wendu knew it and secretly formed a plan to kill Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was displeased; Wendu knew it and secretly plotted to kill him.

sentences.zh: 侗以文都領御史大夫，世充固執而止。

translations.literal: Tong made Wendu oversee the Censorate; Shichong firmly opposed it and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Tong wished to put Wendu in charge of the Censorate, but Shichong firmly blocked it.

sentences.zh: 盧楚說文都誅之，文都遂懷奏入殿。

translations.literal: Lu Chu urged Wendu to kill him; Wendu then entered the hall bearing a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chu urged Wendu to kill Shichong; Wendu then entered the hall with a memorial.

sentences.zh: 有人以告世充，世充馳還含嘉城。

translations.literal: Someone informed Shichong; Shichong galloped back to Jiahe Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed Shichong; he galloped back to Jiahe Fortress.

sentences.zh: 至夜難作，攻東太陽門而入，拜於紫微觀下，曰：「請斬文都，歸罪司寇。

translations.literal: At night trouble arose; he attacked through the East Sun Gate and entered, bowing below the Ziwei Observatory, saying: "I beg to behead Wendu and return the blame to the Minister of Justice."
translations.idiomatic: That night rebellion broke out; he forced the East Sun Gate and entered, bowing below the Ziwei Observatory: "I beg leave to behead Wendu and lay the blame on the Minister of Justice."

sentences.zh: 」侗見兵勢盛，遣其所署將軍黃桃樹執文都以出。

translations.literal: Tong, seeing the troops' strength, sent the general he had appointed, Huang Taoshu, to seize Wendu and bring him out.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the troops' strength, Tong sent his appointed general Huang Taoshu to seize Wendu and hand him over.

sentences.zh: 文都顧謂侗曰：「臣今朝亡，陛下亦當夕及。

translations.literal: Wendu turned and said to Tong: "Your servant dies this morning; Your Majesty will follow this evening."
translations.idiomatic: Wendu turned to Tong and said, "I die this morning; Your Majesty will follow this evening."

sentences.zh: 」侗慟哭遣之，左右莫不憫默。

translations.literal: Tong wept as he sent him forth; those at his side were all silent in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Tong wept as he sent him out; none beside him could speak for grief.

sentences.zh: 出至興教門，世充令左右亂斬之，諸子並見害。

translations.literal: When they reached Xingjiao Gate, Shichong ordered his attendants to hack him to pieces at random; his sons were all killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingjiao Gate Shichong ordered his men to cut Wendu down; his sons were killed as well.

sentences.zh: 則弟矩，字孝矩，西魏時，襲祖爵始平縣公，拜南豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Ze's younger brother Ju, courtesy name Xiaoju, in Western Wei inherited the grandfather's title as Duke of Shiping County and was appointed Governor of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's younger brother Ju, courtesy name Xiaoju, in Western Wei inherited their grandfather's title as Duke of Shiping and was appointed Governor of Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 時見元氏將危，陰謂昆季曰：「宇文之心，路人所見。

translations.literal: Seeing the Yuan clan about to fall, he secretly told his brothers: "The heart of the Yuwen clan is plain to every passerby."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Yuan house about to fall, he secretly told his brothers, "The Yuwen clan's intent is plain to every passerby."

sentences.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用宗子！

translations.literal: "When the house topples and you do not support it—of what use are the sons of the clan!"
translations.idiomatic: "When the house topples and you will not prop it up—what use are the sons of the clan!"

sentences.zh: 」為兄則所遏，乃止。

translations.literal: His elder brother Ze restrained him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ze restrained him, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 後周文為兄子晉公護娶其妹為妻，情好甚密。

translations.literal: Later Zhou Emperor Wen for his nephew the Duke of Jin, Hu, took Ju's younger sister as wife; their affection was very close.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Wen of Zhou took Ju's younger sister as wife for his nephew, the Duke of Jin, Hu; their bond was very close.

sentences.zh: 及護誅，坐徙蜀。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed he was banished to Shu on account of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu was executed Ju was banished to Shu on account of the connection.

sentences.zh: 後拜司憲大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Master of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝重其門地，娶其女為房陵王妃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui valued his family's standing and took his daughter as consort to the Prince of Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui valued his family's standing and married his daughter to the Prince of Fangling.

sentences.zh: 及為丞相，拜少塚宰，位柱國，賜爵洵陽郡公。

translations.literal: When he became Chancellor he was made Junior Director of the Mausoleum, Pillar of State, and granted the title Duke of Xunyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Chancellor he was made Junior Director of the Mausoleum and Pillar of State, and enfeoffed Duke of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 及房陵立為皇太子，立其女為皇太子妃，親禮彌厚，拜夀州總管。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Fangling was established as Crown Prince, his daughter was made Crown Princess; the intimate courtesy grew thicker, and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Shou Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fangling was made crown prince, Ju's daughter became crown princess; favor deepened and he was made Commander-in-Chief of Shou.

sentences.zh: 時陳將任蠻奴等屢寇江北，復以孝矩領行軍總官，屯兵江上。

translations.literal: At that time Chen generals Ren Mannu and others repeatedly raided north of the Yangtze; Xiaoju was again made overall commander on campaign, stationing troops on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen generals such as Ren Mannu repeatedly raided north of the Yangtze, Xiaoju was again made campaign commander-in-chief and stationed troops on the river.

sentences.zh: 後以年老，上表乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Later, because of age, he submitted a memorial begging to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Later, owing to age, he memorialized to retire.

sentences.zh: 輕涇州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子無竭嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wujie inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wujie inherited.

sentences.zh: 矩次弟雅，字孝方，有文武幹用。

translations.literal: Ju's next younger brother Ya, courtesy name Xiaofang, possessed civil and military ability.
translations.idiomatic: Ju's next younger brother Ya, courtesy name Xiaofang, had both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，曆左領左右將軍、集沁二州刺史，封順陽郡公。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he successively served as General of the Left Guard, Governor of Ji and Qin Provinces, and was enfeoffed Duke of Shunyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he served as General of the Left Guard and Governor of Ji and Qin, and was enfeoffed Duke of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 雅弟褒，字孝整，少有成人量。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Bao, courtesy name Xiaozheng, in youth had the measure of a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Bao, courtesy name Xiaozheng, even in youth had the stature of a man grown.

sentences.zh: 年十歲而孤，為諸兄所愛養。

translations.literal: At ten years he was orphaned and was cherished and raised by all his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at ten, he was cherished and raised by all his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 善事諸兄。

translations.literal: He was good to all his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He treated all his elder brothers with devotion.

sentences.zh: 諸兄議欲別居，褒泣諫，不從。

translations.literal: When the elder brothers discussed separating households, Bao wept and remonstrated, but they did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When his brothers discussed dividing the household, Bao wept and remonstrated, but they would not listen.

sentences.zh: 家素富，多金寶，褒一無所受，脫身而出。

translations.literal: The family had long been wealthy with much gold and treasure; Bao accepted none of it and left empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: The family was long wealthy in gold and jewels; Bao took none of it and walked away with nothing.

sentences.zh: 仕周，位開府、北平縣公、趙州刺史。

translations.literal: Serving Zhou he held the rank of Defender-in-Chief, Duke of Beiping County, and Governor of Zhao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Defender-in-Chief, Duke of Beiping, and Governor of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從韋孝寬平尉遲迥，以功拜柱國，進封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Following Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yuchi Jiong, for merit he was made Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yuchi Jiong, he was made Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，拜原州總管。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was made Commander-in-Chief of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was made Commander-in-Chief of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 有商人為賊劫，其人疑同宿者而執之。

translations.literal: A merchant was robbed by bandits; the man suspected a fellow lodger and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: A merchant was robbed by bandits; he suspected a fellow lodger and seized him.

sentences.zh: 褒察其色冤而辭正，遂舍之。

translations.literal: Bao observed that his color showed innocence and his words were upright, and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao saw innocence in his face and uprightness in his words, and released him.

sentences.zh: 商人詣闕訟褒受金縱賊。

translations.literal: The merchant went to the capital to sue Bao for taking gold and releasing the thief.
translations.idiomatic: The merchant went to the capital to accuse Bao of taking gold to let the thief go.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝遣窮之，使者簿責褒何故利金而舍盜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui sent men to investigate thoroughly; the envoy interrogated Bao on why he took profit in gold and released the robber.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent investigators; the envoy pressed Bao on why he had taken gold and freed the robber.

sentences.zh: 褒引咎無異辭。

translations.literal: Bao accepted blame without change in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Bao accepted blame without shifting his story.

sentences.zh: 使者與褒俱詣京師，遂坐免官。

translations.literal: The envoy and Bao both went to the capital; he was thereupon dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy brought Bao to the capital, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 其盜尋發他所。

translations.literal: The thief was soon exposed elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The real thief was soon caught elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「何至自誣？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How could you go so far as to falsely accuse yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why would you go so far as to accuse yourself falsely?"

sentences.zh: 」褒曰：「臣受委一州，不能息盜，臣罪一也；

translations.literal: Bao said: "Your servant received charge of one province and could not quell robbers—my first fault.
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "I was charged with a whole province and could not suppress robbery—that is my first fault.

sentences.zh: 百姓為人所謗，不付法司，懸即放免，臣罪二也；

translations.literal: The common people were slandered by others, yet I did not hand them to the judicial offices and at once released them—my second fault.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner was slandered, yet I did not hand him to the courts and released him at once—that is my second fault.

sentences.zh: 無顧形跡，至今為物所疑，臣罪三也。

translations.literal: Without regard for appearances, I am to this day suspected by others—my third fault.
translations.idiomatic: Without regard for how it looked, I am suspected to this day—that is my third fault.

sentences.zh: 臣有三罪，何所逃責！

translations.literal: Your servant has three faults—what escape from punishment is there!
translations.idiomatic: I have three faults—how could I escape blame!

sentences.zh: 臣又不言受賂，使者復將有所窮究，然則縲絏橫及良善，重臣之罪，是以自誣。

translations.literal: Your servant also did not speak of receiving bribes; the envoy would again have pursued investigation, and then bonds would have spread to touch the innocent—doubling your servant's fault; therefore I falsely accused myself.
translations.idiomatic: Nor did I deny taking a bribe; the envoy would have pressed the inquiry further, and then the innocent would have been dragged into bonds—doubling my fault. That is why I accused myself falsely."

sentences.zh: 」上歎異之，稱為長者。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in wonder and called him an elder of worth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and called him a man of true stature.

sentences.zh: 樂良王萬壽，和平三年封，拜征東大將軍，鎮和龍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yueiang, Wanshou, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and appointed Grand General Campaigning East, garrisoning Helong.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yueiang, Wanshou, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and appointed Grand General Campaigning East, stationed at Helong.

sentences.zh: 性貪暴，征還，道憂薨，諡曰厲王。

translations.literal: Greedy and violent by nature, on the return from campaign he died of grief on the road; his posthumous title was Prince Li.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and violent, he died of distress on the road while returning from campaign; his posthumous name was Prince Li.

sentences.zh: 子康王樂平襲。

translations.literal: His son the Prince of Le, Yueping, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son the Prince of Le, Yueping, inherited.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子長命襲。

translations.literal: His son Changming inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changming inherited.

sentences.zh: 坐殺人賜死，國除。

translations.literal: For killing a man he was granted death; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: For murder he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 子忠，明帝時，復前爵，位太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhong, in Emperor Ming's time, had the former title restored and held the office of Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhong, in Emperor Ming's time, had the former title restored and served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝泛舟天泉池，命宗室諸王陪宴。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu floated on the Tianquan Pool and ordered the princes of the imperial clan to accompany the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu boated on the Tianquan Pool and ordered the imperial princes to join the feast.

sentences.zh: 忠愚而無智，性好衣服，遂著紅羅襦，繡作領，碧綢褲，錦為緣。

translations.literal: Zhong was stupid and without wisdom, and by nature loved clothes; he therefore wore a red silk jacket embroidered at the collar, green silk trousers, and brocade trim.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong was dull and witless and loved fine dress; he wore a red silk jacket with embroidered collar, green silk trousers, and brocade trim.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「朝廷衣冠，應有常式，何為著百戲衣？

translations.literal: The emperor said to him: "Court dress and caps ought to have a fixed form—why wear the clothes of street performers?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Court dress has its proper form—why are you dressed like a street performer?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「臣少來所愛，情存綺羅，歌衣舞服，是臣所願。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "What your servant has loved since youth remains in brocade and gauze; singing robes and dancing garments are what your servant desires."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "What I have loved since youth lives in silk and gauze—singing robes and dancing dress are what I want."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「人之無良乃至此乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That a man can be so without conscience—indeed it reaches this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That a man can be so utterly without shame—it truly comes to this!"

sentences.zh: 廣平王洛侯，和平二年封。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping, Luohou, was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangping, Luohou, was enfeoffed in the second year of Heping.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰殤。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Shang.

sentences.zh: 無子，後以陽平幽王第五子匡後之。

translations.literal: He had no son; later the fifth son of the Prince of Yangping You, Kuang, was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son; later the fifth son of the Prince of Yangping You, Kuang, was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 匡字建扶，性耿介，有氣節。

translations.literal: Kuang, courtesy name Jianfu, was upright and possessed moral fiber.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang, courtesy name Jianfu, was upright and possessed moral fiber.

sentences.zh: 孝文器之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen valued him.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「叔父必能儀形社稷，匡輔朕躬，今可改名為匡，以成克終之美。

translations.literal: He said to him: "Uncle, you will surely be able to set the form of the altars of state and support and assist Our person; now you may change your name to Kuang, to fulfill the beauty of bringing the enterprise to completion."
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "Uncle, you will surely uphold the altars and assist my person; you may now change your name to Kuang—to fulfill the beauty of seeing the work through to the end."

sentences.zh: 」宣武即位，累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne he rose to Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters.

sentences.zh: 茹皓始有寵，百寮微憚之。

translations.literal: Ru Hao first gained favor; the hundred officials slightly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ru Hao first gained favor, the hundred officials feared him somewhat.

sentences.zh: 帝曾于山陵還，詔匡陪乘，又使皓登車。

translations.literal: The emperor once on returning from the mountain tomb ordered Kuang to accompany the carriage, and also had Hao mount the vehicle.
translations.idiomatic: Once, returning from the imperial tombs, the emperor ordered Kuang to ride beside him and also had Hao mount the carriage.

sentences.zh: 皓褰裳將上，匡諫，帝推之令下，皓恨匡失色。

translations.literal: Hao lifted his robe to ascend; Kuang remonstrated; the emperor pushed him down and made him descend; Hao hated Kuang and turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Hao lifted his robe to climb in; Kuang remonstrated; the emperor pushed Hao down; Hao hated Kuang and turned pale.

sentences.zh: 當時壯其忠謇。

translations.literal: At the time they admired his loyal bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all admired his blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 宣武親政，除肆州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu personally took government he was made Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule he was made Governor of Si.

sentences.zh: 匡既忤皓，懼為所害，廉慎自修，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Kuang, having offended Hao, feared being harmed by him and cultivated himself with integrity and caution, gaining a very fine reputation and record.
translations.idiomatic: Having offended Hao, Kuang feared harm and governed with scrupulous integrity, earning a fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 遷恆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Heng.

sentences.zh: 徵為大宗正卿、河南邑中正。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan and Rectifier of the Right for Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Director of the Imperial Clan and Rectifier of the Right for Henan.

sentences.zh: 匡奏親王及始籓、二籓王妻，悉有妃號。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized that imperial princes and the consorts of the founding princes and second-rank princes all ought to have the title of consort.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized that imperial princes' wives and those of the founding and second-rank princes should all bear the title consort.

sentences.zh: 而三籓以下，皆謂之妻。

translations.literal: Yet for princes below the third rank they were all called "wife."
translations.idiomatic: Yet for princes below the third rank they were all called simply "wife."

sentences.zh: 上不得同為妃名，而下不及五品以上有命婦之號，竊以為疑。

translations.literal: Above they could not share the same title of consort, while below they fell short of the fifth rank and above having the title of ennobled lady—he privately regarded this as doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: They could not share the consort title above, yet fell short of the ennobled ladies granted from fifth rank upward—he found this inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夫貴于朝，妻榮于室，婦女無定，升從其夫。

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the husband is honored at court, the wife is glorified in the chamber; for women there is no fixed rank—they rise with their husbands.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "When the husband is honored at court the wife is glorified at home; women have no fixed rank but rise with their husbands.

sentences.zh: 三籓既啟王封，妃名亦宜同等。

translations.literal: The third-rank princes have now opened princely enfeoffment; the title of consort ought likewise to be equal.
translations.idiomatic: Third-rank princes now hold princely fiefs; their consorts' titles should be equal as well.

sentences.zh: 妻者齊也，理與己齊，可從妃例。

translations.literal: Wife means equal; in principle she is equal to oneself—she may follow the consort precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wife means equal—in principle she stands equal to her husband—and may follow the consort precedent.

sentences.zh: 」自是三籓王妻，名號始定。

translations.literal: " From then on the titles of third-rank princes' wives were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the titles of third-rank princes' wives were fixed.

sentences.zh: 從除度支尚書。

translations.literal: He was next made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 匡表引樂陵、章武之例，求紹洛侯封。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized citing the precedents of Leiling and Zhangwu, requesting to continue Luohou's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized citing the precedents of Leiling and Zhangwu, asking to inherit Luohou's fief.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書議。

translations.literal: An edict was sent to the Masters of Writing for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred the matter to the Masters of Writing for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏聽襲封，以明興絕之義。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing memorialized approval of the succession to the fief, to clarify the principle of reviving extinct lines.
translations.idiomatic: This Masters of Writing memorialized approval of the succession to the fief, to clarify the principle of reviving extinct lines.

sentences.zh: 時宣武委政于高肇，宗室傾憚，唯匡與肇抗衡。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xuanwu entrusted government to Gao Zhao; the imperial clan trembled before him—only Kuang stood against Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Xuanwu entrusted government to Gao Zhao; the imperial clan trembled before him—only Kuang stood against Zhao, in the record.

sentences.zh: 先自造棺，置於聽事，意欲輿棺詣闕，論肇罪惡，自殺切諫。

translations.literal: He had earlier had a coffin made and placed in the reception hall, intending to carry it to the palace gate, denounce Zhao's crimes, and kill himself in desperate remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier had a coffin made and placed in the reception hall, intending to carry it to the palace gate, denounce Zhao's crimes; kill himself in desperate remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 肇聞而惡之。

translations.literal: Zhao heard of it and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao heard of it and hated him, in the record.

sentences.zh: 後因與太常卿劉芳議爭權量，遂與肇聲色。

translations.literal: Later, because he disputed weights and measures with Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang, he clashed with Zhao in voice and manner.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he disputed weights and measures with Minister of Ceremonies Liu Fang, he clashed with Zhao in voice and manner, in the record.

sentences.zh: 御史中尉王顯奏匡曰：

translations.literal: Inspector of the Masters of Writing Wang Xian memorialized against Kuang, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of the Masters of Writing Wang Xian memorialized against Kuang, saying:

sentences.zh: 自金行失禦，群偽競興，禮壞樂崩，彝倫攸斁。

translations.literal: Since the Metal dynasty lost the throne, many usurpers rose together; ritual collapsed and music fell into ruin; the great norms were overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Metal dynasty lost the throne, many usurpers rose together; ritual collapsed and music fell into ruin; the great norms were overturned, in the record.

sentences.zh: 高祖孝文皇帝以睿聖統天，克復舊典。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, with sage wisdom ruling heaven, restored the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu Xiaowen, with sage wisdom ruling heaven, restored the old canons, in the record.

sentences.zh: 乃命故中書監高閭，廣旌儒林，推尋樂府，以黍裁寸，將均周、漢舊章。

translations.literal: He then ordered the late Director of the Palace Writers Gao Lu to honor the Confucian schools broadly, search out the Music Office, cut the inch by millet grain, and align with Zhou and Han old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the late Director of the Palace Writers Gao Lu to honor the Confucian schools broadly, search out the Music Office, cut the inch by millet grain; align with Zhou and Han old statutes.

sentences.zh: 屬雲構中遷，尚未雲就。

translations.literal: It happened that the cloud-loom capital moved midway, and the work was not yet complete.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the cloud-loom capital moved midway; the work was not yet complete.

sentences.zh: 高祖睿思玄深，參考經、記，以一黍之大，用成分體，准之為尺，宣佈施行。

translations.literal: Gaozu's wise thought ran deep and dark; consulting classics and records, he took one millet as the measure for fractional parts, made it the standard inch, and promulgated it for use.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's wise thought ran deep and dark; consulting classics and records, he took one millet as the measure for fractional parts, made it the standard inch; promulgated it for use.

sentences.zh: 暨正始中，故太樂令公孫崇輒自立意，以黍十二為寸，別造尺度，定律刊鐘。

translations.literal: By the Zhengshi era the late Director of Music Gongsun Chong on his own authority set twelve grains to the inch, made a separate scale, fixed the laws, and cast the bells.
translations.idiomatic: By the Zhengshi era the late Director of Music Gongsun Chong on his own authority set twelve grains to the inch, made a separate scale, fixed the laws; cast the bells.

sentences.zh: 皆向成訖，表求觀試。

translations.literal: All were nearly finished; he memorialized requesting a trial viewing.
translations.idiomatic: All were nearly finished; he memorialized requesting a trial viewing, in the record.

sentences.zh: 時敕太常卿臣芳，以崇造既成，請集朝英，議其得否。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered Minister of Ceremonies your subject Fang: since Chong's work was done, gather the court's worthies and debate whether it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: At the time an edict ordered Minister of Ceremonies your subject Fang: since Chong's work was done, gather the court's worthies and debate whether it was acceptable, in the record.

sentences.zh: 芳疑崇尺度與先朝不同，察其作者，于經史復異，推造鮮據，非所宜行。

translations.literal: Fang doubted Chong's scale differed from the prior dynasty; examining its makers, it again diverged from classics and histories—forced invention with thin support, not fit to implement.
translations.idiomatic: Fang doubted Chong's scale differed from the prior dynasty; examining its makers, it again diverged from classics and histories—forced invention with thin support, not fit to implement, in the record.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令臣肇、清河王懌等，以崇造乖謬，與《周禮》不同，遂奏臣芳依《周禮》更造，成訖量校，從其善者。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao, Prince of Qinghe Yi, and others, holding Chong's work perverse and unlike the Rites of Zhou, memorialized your subject Fang to remake it per the Zhou Rites; when finished, measure and compare, and follow whichever was better.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao, Prince of Qinghe Yi; others, holding Chong's work perverse and unlike the Rites of Zhou, memorialized your subject Fang to remake it per the Zhou Rites; when finished, measure and compare; follow whichever was better.

sentences.zh: 而芳以先朝尺度，事合古典，乃依前詔書，以黍刊寸，並呈朝廷，用裁金石。

translations.literal: But Fang held the prior dynasty's scale consonant with classical antiquity; he followed the earlier edict, cut the inch by millet, and presented it to court for use in bells and stones.
translations.idiomatic: But Fang held the prior dynasty's scale consonant with classical antiquity; he followed the earlier edict, cut the inch by millet; presented it to court for use in bells and stones.

sentences.zh: 于時議者多雲芳是。

translations.literal: At the time most debaters said Fang was right.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most debaters said Fang was right, in the record.

sentences.zh: 唯黃門侍郎臣孫惠蔚與崇扶同。

translations.literal: Only Yellow Gate Attendant your subject Sun Huiwei sided with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yellow Gate Attendant your subject Sun Huiwei sided with Chong, in the record.

sentences.zh: 二途參差，頻經考議。

translations.literal: The two paths diverged; they were examined again and again.
translations.idiomatic: This two paths diverged; they were examined again and again.

sentences.zh: 而尚書令臣肇以芳造。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao favored Fang's manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Zhao favored Fang's manufacture, in the record.

sentences.zh: 崇物故之後，而惠蔚亦造一尺，仍雲扶。

translations.literal: After Chong died, Huiwei also made a foot-rule, still claiming to support Chong.
translations.idiomatic: After Chong died, Huiwei also made a foot-rule, still claiming to support Chong, in the record.

sentences.zh: 以比崇尺，自相乖背。

translations.literal: Compared with Chong's foot-rule, they contradicted each other.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Chong's foot-rule, they contradicted each other, in the record.

sentences.zh: 量省二三，謂芳一尺為得。

translations.literal: Measuring and checking two or three times, they deemed Fang's foot-rule correct.
translations.idiomatic: Measuring and checking two or three times, they deemed Fang's foot-rule correct, in the record.

sentences.zh: 而尚書臣匡表雲，劉、孫二尺，長短相傾，稽考兩律，所容殊異，言取中黍，校彼二家，雲並參差，折中無所，自立一途，請求議判。

translations.literal: But Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Kuang memorialized that the Liu and Sun foot-rules, long and short leaning against each other, when examined against the two pitch-pipes held different capacities; he said to take the middle millet, compare those two houses, and found both irregular—with no mean to strike, he set up his own path and asked for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: But Director of the Masters of Writing your subject Kuang memorialized that the Liu and Sun foot-rules, long and short leaning against each other, when examined against the two pitch-pipes held different capacities; he said to take the middle millet, compare those two houses; found both irregular—with no mean to strike, he set up his own path and asked for judgment.

sentences.zh: 當時議者，或是于匡，兩途舛駁，未即時定。

translations.literal: Debaters at the time were split for or against Kuang; the two paths clashed and were not settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Debaters at the time were split for or against Kuang; the two paths clashed and were not settled at once, in the record.

sentences.zh: 肇又云：「權斛斗尺，班行已久，今者所論，豈逾先旨，宜仰依先朝故尺為定。」

translations.literal: Zhao also said, "Weights, bushels, pecks, and foot-rules have long been promulgated; what is debated now cannot exceed the prior intent—we should rely on the prior dynasty's old foot-rule as fixed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also said, "Weights, bushels, pecks; foot-rules have long been promulgated; what is debated now cannot exceed the prior intent—we should rely on the prior dynasty's old foot-rule as fixed."

sentences.zh: 自爾以後，而匡與肇厲言都坐，聲色相加，高下失其常倫，尊競無復彝序。

translations.literal: From then on Kuang and Zhao spoke harshly in the imperial audience hall, voices and faces raised against each other; high and low lost their proper order; honor and rivalry knew no ritual sequence.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Kuang and Zhao spoke harshly in the imperial audience hall, voices and faces raised against each other; high and low lost their proper order; honor and rivalry knew no ritual sequence, in the record.

sentences.zh: 匡更表列，據己十是，雲芳十非。

translations.literal: Kuang again memorialized in columns, holding his own ten parts right and Fang's ten parts wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang again memorialized in columns, holding his own ten parts right and Fang's ten parts wrong, in the record.

sentences.zh: 又云：「肇前被敕旨，共芳營督，規立鐘石之名，希播製作之譽。

translations.literal: He also said, "Zhao was earlier charged by edict to supervise jointly with Fang, plotting names for bells and stones, hoping to spread the fame of manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Zhao was earlier charged by edict to supervise jointly with Fang, plotting names for bells and stones, hoping to spread the fame of manufacture, in the record.

sentences.zh: 乃憑樞衡之尊，藉舅氏之勢，與奪任心，臧否自己，阿党劉芳，遏絕臣事。

translations.literal: Relying on the weight of the pivot, borrowing his uncle's power, he judged gain and loss by whim, praise and blame by himself, cliqueing with Liu Fang and blocking your subject's business.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on the weight of the pivot, borrowing his uncle's power, he judged gain and loss by whim, praise and blame by himself, cliqueing with Liu Fang and blocking your subject's business, in the record.

sentences.zh: 望勢雷同者，接以恩言；

translations.literal: Those who echoed power he greeted with gracious words;
translations.idiomatic: Those who echoed power he greeted with gracious words;

sentences.zh: 依經案古者，即被怒責。

translations.literal: those who checked classics against antiquity were at once rebuked in anger.
translations.idiomatic: those who checked classics against antiquity were at once rebuked in anger, in the record.

sentences.zh: 雖未指鹿化馬，移天徙日，實使蘊藉之士，聳氣坐端；

translations.literal: Though he has not yet turned deer into horses or moved heaven and shifted the sun, he truly makes refined gentlemen stiffen with fear at their seats;
translations.idiomatic: Though he has not yet turned deer into horses or moved heaven and shifted the sun, he truly makes refined gentlemen stiffen with fear at their seats;

sentences.zh: 懷道之夫，結舌筵次。

translations.literal: men who cherish the Way bite their tongues at the feast.
translations.idiomatic: men who cherish the Way bite their tongues at the feast, in the record.

sentences.zh: 」又言「芳昔與崇競，恆言自作，今共臣論，忽稱先朝。

translations.literal: He also said, "Fang once competed with Chong and always said he made it himself; now debating with your subject he suddenly cites the prior dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Fang once competed with Chong and always said he made it himself; now debating with your subject he suddenly cites the prior dynasty, in the record.

sentences.zh: 豈不前謂可行，輒欲自取；

translations.literal: Did he not first say it would work and at once seek to take credit himself;
translations.idiomatic: Did he not first say it would work and at once seek to take credit himself;

sentences.zh: 後知錯謬，便推先朝。

translations.literal: then, knowing it wrong, push it onto the prior dynasty?
translations.idiomatic: then, knowing it wrong, push it onto the prior dynasty?

sentences.zh: 殊非大臣之體，深失為下之義。

translations.literal: This is far from a great minister's bearing and deeply fails the duty of a subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: This is far from a great minister's bearing and deeply fails the duty of a subordinate, in the record.

sentences.zh: 復考校勢臣之前，量度偏頗之手，臣必刖足內朝，抱璞人外。

translations.literal: To re-examine before powerful ministers and measure in the hands of the partial—your subject would surely lose his feet in the inner court and hold his jade outside the gate."
translations.idiomatic: To re-examine before powerful ministers and measure in the hands of the partial—your subject would surely lose his feet in the inner court and hold his jade outside the gate."

sentences.zh: 」囂言肆意，彰於朝野。

translations.literal: His clamor ran wild, plain to court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: His clamor ran wild, plain to court and countryside, in the record.

sentences.zh: 然匡職當出納，獻替所在，鬥尺權度，正是所司。

translations.literal: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and output; remonstrance and replacement were his place; pecks, foot-rules, weights, and measures were precisely his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Kuang's duty was intake and output; remonstrance and replacement were his place; pecks, foot-rules, weights; measures were precisely his office.

sentences.zh: 若己有所見，能練臧否，宜應首唱義端，早辨諸惑，何故默心隨從，不關一言，見芳成事，方出此語？

translations.literal: If he had a view of his own and could judge right and wrong, he ought to have led with the righteous point and early cleared all doubts—why keep silent in heart and follow, not speaking one word, and only after Fang's work was done utter this?
translations.idiomatic: If he had a view of his own and could judge right and wrong, he ought to have led with the righteous point and early cleared all doubts—why keep silent in heart and follow, not speaking one word; only after Fang's work was done utter this?

sentences.zh: 計芳才學，與匡殊懸，所見淺深，不應相匹。

translations.literal: Considering Fang's talent and learning, he and Kuang are worlds apart in depth of insight—they should not be matched.
translations.idiomatic: Considering Fang's talent and learning, he and Kuang are worlds apart in depth of insight—they should not be matched, in the record.

sentences.zh: 今乃始發，恐此由心，借智於人，規成虛譽。

translations.literal: That he speaks only now—fear this comes from the heart, borrowing others' wisdom to build empty fame.
translations.idiomatic: That he speaks only now—fear this comes from the heart, borrowing others' wisdom to build empty fame, in the record.

sentences.zh: 況匡表云：「所據銅權，形如古志，明是漢作，非莽別造。

translations.literal: Moreover Kuang's memorial said, "The bronze weight I rely on matches ancient records in form; clearly it is Han work, not a separate creation of Mang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Kuang's memorial said, "The bronze weight I rely on matches ancient records in form; clearly it is Han work, not a separate creation of Mang, in the record.

sentences.zh: 」及案權銘，「黃帝始祖，德布于虞；

translations.literal: " Examining the weight's inscription: "Yellow Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Yu;

translations.literal: Yu Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Xin."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Emperor the founding ancestor—his virtue spread in Xin."

sentences.zh: 若莽佐漢時事，寧有銘偽新之號哉？

translations.literal: If this were Mang aiding Han times, how could the inscription bear the false title Xin?
translations.idiomatic: If this were Mang aiding Han times, how could the inscription bear the false title Xin?

sentences.zh: 又尋莽傳，雲莽居攝，即變漢制度。

translations.literal: Searching Mang's biography, it says when Mang held the regency he at once changed Han institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Searching Mang's biography, it says when Mang held the regency he at once changed Han institutions, in the record.

sentences.zh: 考校二證，非漢權明矣。

translations.literal: Checking the two proofs, clearly it is not a Han weight.
translations.idiomatic: Checking the two proofs, clearly it is not a Han weight, in the record.

sentences.zh: 復云「芳之所造，又短先朝之尺。

translations.literal: He also said, "What Fang made is again shorter than the prior dynasty's foot-rule.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "What Fang made is again shorter than the prior dynasty's foot-rule, in the record.

sentences.zh: 臣既比之，權然相合。

translations.literal: Your subject has compared them; the weight agrees exactly.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has compared them; the weight agrees exactly, in the record.

sentences.zh: 更云「芳尺與千金堰不同。

translations.literal: He further said, "Fang's foot-rule differs from the Qianjin weir."
translations.idiomatic: He further said, "Fang's foot-rule differs from the Qianjin weir."

sentences.zh: 」臣復量比，因見其異，二三浮濫，難可據准。

translations.literal: Your subject again measured and compared and saw the difference—two or three parts floating loose, hard to use as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject again measured and compared and saw the difference—two or three parts floating loose, hard to use as standard, in the record.

sentences.zh: 又云「共構虛端，妄為疑似，托以先朝，雲非己制」。

translations.literal: He also said, "They jointly built empty ends, falsely made suspicion, claiming the prior dynasty and saying it was not their own manufacture."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "They jointly built empty ends, falsely made suspicion, claiming the prior dynasty and saying it was not their own manufacture."

sentences.zh: 臣案此欺詐，乃在於匡，不在於芳。

translations.literal: Your subject finds this fraud lies in Kuang, not in Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject finds this fraud lies in Kuang, not in Fang, in the record.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 芳先被敕，專造鐘律，管籥優劣，是其所裁，權斛尺度，本非其事。

translations.literal: Fang was first charged by edict to specialize in bells and pitch-pipes; the excellence of tubes and reeds was his to judge—weights, bushels, and foot-rules were never his affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was first charged by edict to specialize in bells and pitch-pipes; the excellence of tubes and reeds was his to judge—weights, bushels; foot-rules were never his affair.

sentences.zh: 比前門下索芳尺度，而芳牒報云「依先朝所班新尺，復應下黍，更不增損，為造鐘律，調正分寸而已」。

translations.literal: Earlier the Palace Secretariat sought Fang's scale; Fang's reply said, "Following the new foot-rule promulgated by the prior dynasty, again applying the lower millet without further increase or decrease—only adjusting fractional parts to make bells and pitch-pipes."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Palace Secretariat sought Fang's scale; Fang's reply said, "Following the new foot-rule promulgated by the prior dynasty, again applying the lower millet without further increase or decrease—only adjusting fractional parts to make bells and pitch-pipes."

sentences.zh: 檢匡造時，在牒後一歲，芳於爾日，匡未共爭，已有此牒，豈為詐也？

translations.literal: Checking when Kuang made his rule, it was one year after that reply; on that day Fang and Kuang had not yet disputed—this reply already existed. How call it fraud?
translations.idiomatic: Checking when Kuang made his rule, it was one year after that reply; on that day Fang and Kuang had not yet disputed—this reply already existed. How call it fraud?

sentences.zh: 計崇造寸，積黍十二，群情共知。

translations.literal: Chong's inch used twelve stacked grains—everyone knows it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's inch used twelve stacked grains—everyone knows it, in the record.

sentences.zh: 而芳造寸，唯止十黍，亦俱見。

translations.literal: Fang's inch used only ten grains—also plain to all.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's inch used only ten grains—also plain to all, in the record.

sentences.zh: 先朝詔書，以黍成寸，首尾曆然，寧有輒欲自取之理？

translations.literal: The prior dynasty's edict, making the inch from millet, is clear from start to finish—how could there be a reason to seize it for oneself?
translations.idiomatic: This prior dynasty's edict, making the inch from millet, is clear from start to finish—how could there be a reason to seize it for oneself?

sentences.zh: 肇任居端右，百寮是望，言行動靜，必副具瞻。

translations.literal: Zhao holds the foremost right seat; the hundred offices look to him—word, act, movement, and stillness must match what all watch.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao holds the foremost right seat; the hundred offices look to him—word, act, movement; stillness must match what all watch.

sentences.zh: 若恃權阿黨，詐托先詔，將指鹿化馬，徙日移天，即是魏之趙高，何以宰物？

translations.literal: If he relies on power, cliques, and fraudulently claims the prior edict, turning deer into horses and shifting sun and day—he is Zhao Gao of Wei; how can he govern things?
translations.idiomatic: If he relies on power, cliques; fraudulently claims the prior edict, turning deer into horses and shifting sun and day—he is Zhao Gao of Wei; how can he govern things?

sentences.zh: 肇若無此，匡既誣毀宰相，訕謗時政，阻惑朝聽，不敬至甚。

translations.literal: If Zhao has none of this, Kuang has slandered the chancellor, mocked current policy, blocked the court's hearing—impiety in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhao has none of this, Kuang has slandered the chancellor, mocked current policy, blocked the court's hearing—impiety in the extreme, in the record.

sentences.zh: 請以肇、匡並禁尚書，推窮其原，付廷尉定罪。

translations.literal: We ask that Zhao and Kuang both be barred from the Masters of Writing, the root traced to the end, and the case sent to the Minister of Justice for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Zhao and Kuang both be barred from the Masters of Writing, the root traced to the end; the case sent to the Minister of Justice for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 詔曰「可」。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Approved."

sentences.zh: 有司奏匡誣肇，處匡死刑。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized that Kuang had slandered Zhao and sentenced Kuang to death.
translations.idiomatic: This relevant offices memorialized that Kuang had slandered Zhao and sentenced Kuang to death.

sentences.zh: 宣武恕死，降為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu spared his life and reduced him to Honored Grandee of Light.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu spared his life and reduced him to Honored Grandee of Light, in the record.

sentences.zh: 又兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: He was also made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Grand Master of the Imperial Clan, in the record.

sentences.zh: 出為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Yanzhou, in the record.

sentences.zh: 匡臨發，帝引見於東堂，勞勉之。

translations.literal: As Kuang was about to depart, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: As Kuang was about to depart, the emperor received him in the Eastern Hall and comforted him, in the record.

sentences.zh: 匡猶以尺度金石之事，國之大經，前雖為南台所彈，然猶許更議。

translations.literal: Kuang still held that scales, foot-rules, bells, and stones were great statutes of state; though the Southern Terrace had impeached him before, he was still allowed further debate.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang still held that scales, foot-rules, bells; stones were great statutes of state; though the Southern Terrace had impeached him before, he was still allowed further debate.

sentences.zh: 若議之日，願聽臣暫赴。

translations.literal: If there is a day of debate, I beg leave to attend briefly.
translations.idiomatic: If there is a day of debate, I beg leave to attend briefly, in the record.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「劉芳學高一時，深明典故。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Liu Fang's learning tops his age; he is deep in ancient precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This emperor said, "Liu Fang's learning tops his age; he is deep in ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 其所據者，與先朝尺乃寸過一黍，何得復雲先朝之意也？

translations.literal: What he relies on differs from the prior dynasty's foot-rule by only one millet per inch—how can he again say it is the prior dynasty's intent?"
translations.idiomatic: What he relies on differs from the prior dynasty's foot-rule by only one millet per inch—how can he again say it is the prior dynasty's intent?"

sentences.zh: 兗州既所執不經，後議之日，何待赴都也。」

translations.literal: Yanzhou is already what you hold without warrant; on the day of later debate, why wait to come to the capital?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou is already what you hold without warrant; on the day of later debate, why wait to come to the capital?"

sentences.zh: 明帝初，入為御史中尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he entered as Inspector of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he entered as Inspector of the Masters of Writing, in the record.

sentences.zh: 匡嚴於彈糾，始奏於忠，次彈高聰等免官，靈太后並不許。

translations.literal: Kuang was severe in impeachment; he first memorialized against Yu Zhong, then against Gao Cong and others for removal—all were denied by Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was severe in impeachment; he first memorialized against Yu Zhong, then against Gao Cong and others for removal—all were denied by Empress Dowager Ling, in the record.

sentences.zh: 違其糾惡之心，又慮匡辭解，欲獎安之，進號安南將軍，後加鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: Thwarted in his wish to impeach the wicked, and fearing Kuang would resign, she wished to reward and reassure him—advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, later added General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Thwarted in his wish to impeach the wicked; fearing Kuang would resign, she wished to reward and reassure him—advanced to General Who Pacifies the South, later added General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 匡每有奏請，尚書令、任城王澄時致執奪。

translations.literal: Whenever Kuang had a memorial request, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Rencheng Cheng would often seize and block it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Kuang had a memorial request, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince of Rencheng Cheng would often seize and block it, in the record.

sentences.zh: 匡剛隘，內遂不平。

translations.literal: Kuang was harsh and narrow; inwardly he grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was harsh and narrow; inwardly he grew resentful, in the record.

sentences.zh: 先所造棺，猶在僧寺，乃復修事，將與澄相攻。

translations.literal: The coffin he had made earlier was still at a monastery; he again prepared matters, intending to clash with Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: This coffin he had made earlier was still at a monastery; he again prepared matters, intending to clash with Cheng.

sentences.zh: 澄頗知之，後將赴省，與匡逢遇，騶卒相撾，朝野駭愕。

translations.literal: Cheng learned of it somewhat; later, going to the Secretariat, he met Kuang by chance—their outriders beat each other; court and countryside were appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng learned of it somewhat; later, going to the Secretariat, he met Kuang by chance—their outriders beat each other; court and countryside were appalled, in the record.

sentences.zh: 澄因是奏匡罪狀三十餘條，廷尉處以死刑。

translations.literal: Cheng therefore memorialized more than thirty counts against Kuang; the Minister of Justice sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng therefore memorialized more than thirty counts against Kuang; the Minister of Justice sentenced him to death, in the record.

sentences.zh: 詔付八議，特加原宥，削爵除官。

translations.literal: An edict referred it to the eightfold deliberation; he was specially pardoned, stripped of rank and office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict referred it to the eightfold deliberation; he was specially pardoned, stripped of rank and office, in the record.

sentences.zh: 三公郎中辛雄奏理之。

translations.literal: Senior Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Xin Xiong memorialized to judge the case.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Xin Xiong memorialized to judge the case, in the record.

sentences.zh: 後特除平州刺史，徙青州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was specially appointed governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was specially appointed governor of Pingzhou, then transferred to Qingzhou, in the record.

sentences.zh: 尋為關右都督、兼尚書行台。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Commander of the Guanxi region and acting Director of the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Commander of the Guanxi region and acting Director of the Masters of Writing on the Mobile Office, in the record.

sentences.zh: 遇疾，還京。

translations.literal: He fell ill and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and returned to the capital, in the record.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，卒，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died; posthumous name Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning of Xiaochang he died; posthumous name Wen Zhen, in the record.

sentences.zh: 後追復本爵，改封濟南王。

translations.literal: Later his original rank was posthumously restored and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Later his original rank was posthumously restored and he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jinan, in the record.
